What `with` really does (desugaring)★★★ · ex04_with_desugared

context_managers.exit, context_managers.enter

Problem

Implement the with statement by hand - no with, no contextlib, no ExitStack.

  1. run_with(cm, body) -> result | None behaves exactly like: def f(): with cm as value: return body(value)

    • enter / exit are looked up on type(cm), not on the instance (like the interpreter). If either is missing -> TypeError, and nothing is called.
    • exit is called exactly once:
      • body succeeded -> exit(None, None, None); return body's result
      • body raised e -> exit(type(e), e, e.traceback) truthy return -> exception swallowed, run_with returns None falsy -> re-raise the ORIGINAL exception (bare raise) This holds for BaseExceptions too (KeyboardInterrupt reaches exit).
    • if enter raises, exit is NOT called
    • if exit itself raises, that new exception propagates (Python chains the original one as its context automatically)

  2. run_nested(cms, body) -> result | None behaves like with cms[0] as v0, cms[1] as v1, ...: return body([v0, v1, ...])

    • enter left to right, exit right to left
    • each exit sees the exception that is current at that point: if an inner one swallowed it, the outer ones get (None, None, None); if an inner one raised a new exception, the outer ones see the new one
    • if entering cms[k] fails, cms[k-1] ... cms[0] are exited with that exception
    • empty cms -> body([]) (hint: it's a few lines on top of run_with)

Interviewers look for

  • Precise protocol knowledge: special-method lookup on the type, the 3 exit arguments, truthiness of exit's return value, enter failure semantics, reverse exit order.
  • How an exception inside exit replaces the original (and how context keeps it).
  • This is exactly what ExitStack implements generically.

Work in exercises/py/12_context_managers/ex04_with_desugared.py (or copy the starter code into any scratch file).

from collections.abc import Callable, Sequence
from typing import Any, TypeVar
R = TypeVar('R')

def run_with(cm: Any, body: Callable[[Any], R]) -> R | None:
    raise NotImplementedError

def run_nested(cms: Sequence[Any], body: Callable[[list[Any]], R]) -> R | None:
    raise NotImplementedError

from collections.abc import Callable, Sequence
from typing import Any, TypeVar

R = TypeVar("R")


def run_with(cm: Any, body: Callable[[Any], R]) -> R | None:
    cls = type(cm)
    try:
        enter = cls.__enter__
        exit_ = cls.__exit__
    except AttributeError:
        raise TypeError(f"{cls.__name__!r} object does not support the context manager protocol") from None
    value = enter(cm)
    try:
        result = body(value)
    except BaseException as e:
        if not exit_(cm, type(e), e, e.__traceback__):
            raise
        return None
    exit_(cm, None, None, None)
    return result


def run_nested(cms: Sequence[Any], body: Callable[[list[Any]], R]) -> R | None:
    if not cms:
        return body([])
    first, rest = cms[0], cms[1:]
    return run_with(first, lambda v: run_nested(rest, lambda vs: body([v, *vs])))

ExitStack: N resources, partial failure, handoff★★★ · ex05_exitstack_resources

context_managers.cleanup, context_managers.custom

Problem

You can't write with open(a), open(b), ... when the number of resources is only known at runtime (N output shards, N model clients). contextlib.ExitStack solves that.

  1. open_shards(directory, n, *, prefix="shard") - context manager

    • opens n files directory/f"{prefix}-{i:05d}.jsonl" for writing (UTF-8) and yields the list of file objects
    • if opening file k fails, files 0..k-1 are closed and the error propagates
    • all files are closed when the block exits (normally or with an exception)
    • n < 1 -> ValueError

  2. class ShardedWriter(directory, n)

    • with ShardedWriter(d, 4) as w: opens the shards (reuse open_shards or an ExitStack directly); w.write(record: dict) appends one JSON line, round-robin over the shards: record 0 -> shard 0, record 1 -> shard 1, ...
    • w.counts -> list[int] records written per shard
    • exit closes everything and never swallows exceptions
    • if enter fails half-way, nothing stays open

  3. acquire_all(factories) -> list

    • calls each factory() to create a client (objects with .close())
    • if factory k raises: close the clients 0..k-1 in REVERSE order, re-raise
    • on success return all clients OPEN - ownership passes to the caller (hint: ExitStack.callback + pop_all())

Interviewers look for

  • ExitStack.enter_context / callback / push, LIFO unwind, and pop_all() to transfer ownership out of a "construct or clean up" block.
  • Partial-failure cleanup: the bug where file #7 fails to open and #0-#6 leak.
  • Implementing enter/exit on a class by delegating to an internal ExitStack.

Work in exercises/py/12_context_managers/ex05_exitstack_resources.py (or copy the starter code into any scratch file).

import json
from collections.abc import Callable, Iterator, Sequence
from contextlib import ExitStack, contextmanager
from pathlib import Path
from types import TracebackType
from typing import IO, Any, Protocol, TypeVar


class Closeable(Protocol):
    def close(self) -> object: ...


C = TypeVar("C", bound=Closeable)


@contextmanager
def open_shards(directory: str | Path, n: int, *, prefix: str = "shard") -> Iterator[list[IO[str]]]:
    if n < 1:
        raise ValueError("n must be >= 1")
    directory = Path(directory)
    with ExitStack() as stack:
        files: list[IO[str]] = [
            stack.enter_context(open(directory / f"{prefix}-{i:05d}.jsonl", "w", encoding="utf-8"))
            for i in range(n)
        ]
        yield files


class ShardedWriter:
    def __init__(self, directory: str | Path, n: int) -> None:
        self.directory = Path(directory)
        self.n = n
        self.counts: list[int] = [0] * n
        self._files: list[IO[str]] = []
        self._stack: ExitStack | None = None
        self._next = 0

    def __enter__(self) -> "ShardedWriter":
        with ExitStack() as stack:
            self._files = stack.enter_context(open_shards(self.directory, self.n))
            self._stack = stack.pop_all()  # success: keep everything open
        self.counts = [0] * self.n
        self._next = 0
        return self

    def write(self, record: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        i = self._next
        self._files[i].write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
        self.counts[i] += 1
        self._next = (i + 1) % self.n

    def __exit__(
        self,
        exc_type: type[BaseException] | None,
        exc: BaseException | None,
        tb: TracebackType | None,
    ) -> None:
        stack, self._stack = self._stack, None
        if stack is not None:
            stack.close()


def acquire_all(factories: Sequence[Callable[[], C]]) -> list[C]:
    with ExitStack() as stack:
        clients: list[C] = []
        for factory in factories:
            client = factory()
            stack.callback(client.close)
            clients.append(client)
        stack.pop_all()  # nothing failed: caller now owns the clients
    return clients

Python Modules and Packages

Parsing requirements.txt★☆☆ · ex01_requirements_parser

Problem

Before a deploy you want to lint requirements.txt: are all versions pinned? Write a small parser for the common subset of the PEP 508 / pip format (no packaging library).

# LLM stack
openai==1.51.0
LangChain_Core >= 0.3, <0.4      # loose!
uvicorn[standard,  socks]==0.30.6
uvloop==0.20.0 ; sys_platform != "win32"
mypkg @ https://example.com/mypkg-1.0.tar.gz
-r dev-requirements.txt
--index-url https://pypi.org/simple
numpy==2.1.1 \
    --hash=sha256:abc

  1. normalize_name(name) -> str PEP 503: lower-case, runs of "-", "_", "." become one "-" ("LangChain_Core" -> "langchain-core")

  2. parse_requirement(line) -> Requirement | None (Requirement dataclass is given)

    • comments: "#" at the start of the line or preceded by whitespace starts a comment
    • blank / comment-only lines and pip option lines (starting with "-") -> None
    • NAME [ "[" extras "]" ] [ SPECIFIER | "@" URL ] [ ";" MARKER ]
      • name normalized; extras normalized, de-duplicated, sorted tuple
      • specifier: comma-separated clauses, each OP VERSION with OP in ~= == != <= >= < > === ; returned with ALL whitespace removed (">=0.3,<0.4"), "" if absent
      • url: text after "@" (stripped) or None; marker: text after the first ";" (stripped) or None
      • any trailing pip per-requirement options ("--hash=...") are dropped
    • anything malformed (no name, unclosed "[", a bad specifier clause such as "=1.0" or ">=") -> ValueError mentioning the line

  3. parse_requirements(text) -> list[Requirement]

    • a line ending in "\" continues on the next line; None results are skipped

  4. unpinned(reqs) -> list[str] names (in order) whose specifier is not exactly one "==" clause without wildcard ("==1.*" is not a pin) and that are not URL requirements

Interviewers look for

  • requirements.txt is pip input: it can be a loose list or a fully pinned lock (pip freeze / pip-compile output). Know the difference and why deploys need pins (+ hashes) while libraries declare ranges.
  • Name normalization - "LangChain_Core" and "langchain-core" are the same project.
  • Environment markers for platform-specific deps; extras for optional features.

Work in exercises/py/13_packaging/ex01_requirements_parser.py (or copy the starter code into any scratch file).

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Requirement:
    name: str
    extras: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    specifier: str = ""
    marker: str | None = None
    url: str | None = None


def normalize_name(name: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"[-_.]+", "-", name).lower()


def _strip_comment(line: str) -> str:
    m = re.search(r"(^|\s)#", line)
    return line[: m.start()] if m else line


def parse_requirement(line: str) -> Requirement | None:
    text = _strip_comment(line).strip()
    if not text or text.startswith("-"):
        return None
    text = re.split(r"\s--\S", " " + text, maxsplit=1)[0].strip()  # drop --hash=... etc.

    m = re.match(r"^([A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9._-]*[A-Za-z0-9])?)\s*(.*)$", text, re.S)
    if not m:
        raise ValueError(f"invalid requirement (no name): {line!r}")
    name, rest = m.group(1), m.group(2).strip()

    extras: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    if rest.startswith("["):
        end = rest.find("]")
        if end == -1:
            raise ValueError(f"unclosed extras in: {line!r}")
        items = {normalize_name(e.strip()) for e in rest[1:end].split(",") if e.strip()}
        extras = tuple(sorted(items))
        rest = rest[end + 1 :].strip()

    marker = None
    if ";" in rest:
        rest, marker = (part.strip() for part in rest.split(";", 1))
        marker = marker or None

    url = None
    specifier = ""
    if rest.startswith("@"):
        url = rest[1:].strip() or None
        if url is None:
            raise ValueError(f"missing URL after '@' in: {line!r}")
    elif rest:
        clauses = [c.strip() for c in rest.split(",")]
        for clause in clauses:
            if not re.match(r"^(~=|===|==|!=|<=|>=|<|>)\s*([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9.*+!_-]*)$", clause):
                raise ValueError(f"invalid specifier {clause!r} in: {line!r}")
        specifier = ",".join(re.sub(r"\s+", "", c) for c in clauses)

    return Requirement(normalize_name(name), extras, specifier, marker, url)


def parse_requirements(text: str) -> list[Requirement]:
    joined = re.sub(r"\\\r?\n", " ", text)  # backslash line continuations
    reqs = (parse_requirement(line) for line in joined.splitlines())
    return [r for r in reqs if r is not None]


def unpinned(reqs: list[Requirement]) -> list[str]:
    out: list[str] = []
    for r in reqs:
        if r.url is not None:
            continue
        clauses = r.specifier.split(",") if r.specifier else []
        pinned = len(clauses) == 1 and clauses[0].startswith("==") and "*" not in clauses[0]
        if not pinned:
            out.append(r.name)
    return out

pyproject.toml dependencies & the environment★★☆ · ex02_pyproject_and_env

Problem

A CI step must answer "does the active environment satisfy this project?".

  1. load_project(path) -> ProjectInfo (ProjectInfo dataclass is given)

    • parse pyproject.toml with tomllib (stdlib 3.11+)
    • name, version (None if missing - e.g. dynamic), requires_python (None if missing), dependencies ([project].dependencies, default []), optional ([project.optional-dependencies], default {}), groups ([dependency-groups] - PEP 735, default {})
    • no [project] table -> ValueError
    • dependency-group entries may be {include-group = "other"} tables: resolve them (recursively, in place, keeping order); unknown group or a cycle -> ValueError

  2. collect_requirements(info, extras=(), groups=()) -> list[str] dependencies + the requested extras + the requested groups, in that order, exact duplicates removed (first occurrence wins); unknown extra/group -> KeyError

  3. requirement_name(req: str) -> str the normalized project name at the start of a requirement string ("Pydantic[email]>=2 ; python_version>'3.9'" -> "pydantic")

  4. check_installed(requirements, installed: Mapping[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]

    • installed maps project name -> version (names may be un-normalized)
    • returns problems only: {name: "missing"} or, for an exact pin "name==X" whose installed version differs, {name: "installed Y, required ==X"} (other specifiers: only presence is checked)

  5. installed_versions() -> dict[str, str] normalized name -> version of every distribution in the running environment (importlib.metadata)

  6. environment_info() -> dict[str, object] keys: "in_venv" (bool: sys.prefix != sys.base_prefix), "prefix", "base_prefix", "executable" (sys.executable), "site_packages" (sysconfig purelib path)

Interviewers look for

  • pyproject.toml as THE config file (PEP 621 metadata, build-system, tool config); [project.dependencies] = what the package needs (ranges), lock files = what an app deploys (exact). Extras vs dependency groups (dev tools aren't published).
  • tomllib.load needs a BINARY file object ("rb") - a frequent TypeError.
  • How a venv works: its own prefix + site-packages; sys.prefix != sys.base_prefix; "activate" just puts its bin/ first on PATH.
  • importlib.metadata to inspect what's installed (what pip freeze reads).

import importlib.metadata
import re
import sys
import sysconfig
import tomllib
from collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any


@dataclass
class ProjectInfo:
    name: str
    version: str | None = None
    requires_python: str | None = None
    dependencies: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    optional: dict[str, list[str]] = field(default_factory=dict)
    groups: dict[str, list[str]] = field(default_factory=dict)


def _resolve_group(
    name: str, raw: Mapping[str, list[Any]], done: dict[str, list[str]], stack: tuple[str, ...]
) -> list[str]:
    if name in done:
        return done[name]
    if name in stack:
        raise ValueError(f"dependency-group cycle: {' -> '.join((*stack, name))}")
    if name not in raw:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown dependency group {name!r}")
    out: list[str] = []
    for entry in raw[name]:
        if isinstance(entry, dict):
            out.extend(_resolve_group(entry["include-group"], raw, done, (*stack, name)))
        else:
            out.append(entry)
    done[name] = out
    return out


def load_project(path: str | Path) -> ProjectInfo:
    with open(path, "rb") as f:  # tomllib requires bytes
        data = tomllib.load(f)
    project = data.get("project")
    if project is None:
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: no [project] table")
    raw_groups = data.get("dependency-groups", {})
    resolved: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for g in raw_groups:
        _resolve_group(g, raw_groups, resolved, ())
    return ProjectInfo(
        name=project["name"],
        version=project.get("version"),
        requires_python=project.get("requires-python"),
        dependencies=list(project.get("dependencies", [])),
        optional={k: list(v) for k, v in project.get("optional-dependencies", {}).items()},
        groups={g: resolved[g] for g in raw_groups},
    )


def collect_requirements(
    info: ProjectInfo, extras: Iterable[str] = (), groups: Iterable[str] = ()
) -> list[str]:
    reqs = list(info.dependencies)
    for extra in extras:
        reqs += info.optional[extra]
    for group in groups:
        reqs += info.groups[group]
    return list(dict.fromkeys(reqs))  # ordered de-duplication


def _normalize(name: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"[-_.]+", "-", name).lower()


def requirement_name(req: str) -> str:
    m = re.match(r"\s*([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*)", req)
    if not m:
        raise ValueError(f"invalid requirement: {req!r}")
    return _normalize(m.group(1).rstrip("._-"))


def check_installed(requirements: Iterable[str], installed: Mapping[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    have = {_normalize(k): v for k, v in installed.items()}
    problems: dict[str, str] = {}
    for req in requirements:
        name = requirement_name(req)
        if name not in have:
            problems[name] = "missing"
            continue
        spec = req.split(";", 1)[0]
        pin = re.search(r"(?<![=!<>~])==\s*([^\s,;]+)\s*$", spec)
        if pin and have[name] != pin.group(1):
            problems[name] = f"installed {have[name]}, required =={pin.group(1)}"
    return problems


def installed_versions() -> dict[str, str]:
    return {
        _normalize(dist.metadata["Name"]): dist.version
        for dist in importlib.metadata.distributions()
        if dist.metadata["Name"]
    }


def environment_info() -> dict[str, object]:
    return {
        "in_venv": sys.prefix != sys.base_prefix,
        "prefix": sys.prefix,
        "base_prefix": sys.base_prefix,
        "executable": sys.executable,
        "site_packages": sysconfig.get_paths()["purelib"],
    }

Problem

write_package(root: Path) -> Path Create this package under root (write the files; return root / "ragkit"):

ragkit/
├── __init__.py        __version__ = "0.1.0"
│                      re-exports chunk and embed;  __all__ = ["chunk", "embed", "__version__"]
│                      must NOT import ragkit.cli (importing the library must stay cheap)
├── _internal.py       SECRET = 42      (private: not re-exported)
├── embed.py           embed(text: str) -> list[int]: the length of each chunk of size 4,
│                      e.g. embed("abcdefghij") == [4, 4, 2]; gets `chunk` via a
│                      RELATIVE import
├── text/
│   ├── __init__.py    re-exports chunk (relative import)
│   └── chunking.py    chunk(text: str, size: int) -> list[str]  (fixed-size slices;
│                      size <= 0 -> ValueError)
├── cli.py             main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int
│                        prints f"ragkit {__version__}" (version imported relatively),
│                        returns 0; plus a __name__ == "__main__" guard that does
│                        raise SystemExit(main())
└── __main__.py        makes `python -m ragkit` call cli.main() the same way

Rules the tests check (behaviour, not your exact text): * import ragkit works with root on sys.path, and does not import ragkit.cli * from ragkit import * binds exactly chunk, embed, version * every intra-package import is relative: a copy of the directory renamed to "ragkit_fork" must import and work WITHOUT the original "ragkit" importable * importing ragkit.cli prints nothing; running it as a script / with -m prints the version * python -m ragkit prints "ragkit 0.1.0" and exits with code 0

Interviewers look for

  • Module = one .py file; package = a directory with init.py (regular) - or without (namespace package). init.py runs on first import of the package: keep it light.
  • __all__ controls from pkg import * and documents the public API.
  • Relative imports (from .text.chunking import chunk) only work inside a package (__package__ set) - running a module file directly breaks them; use python -m.
  • if __name__ == "__main__": - the module's name is "main" only when executed as the entry point; __main__.py is what python -m package runs.

from pathlib import Path

def write_package(root: Path) -> Path:
    raise NotImplementedError

from pathlib import Path


def _sources() -> dict[str, str]:
    # in a private helper so the stub doesn't ship the answer
    return {
        "__init__.py": '''\
"""ragkit - a toy RAG toolkit."""

from .embed import embed
from .text import chunk

__version__ = "0.1.0"
__all__ = ["chunk", "embed", "__version__"]
''',
        "_internal.py": "SECRET = 42\n",
        "embed.py": """\
from .text.chunking import chunk


def embed(text: str) -> list[int]:
    return [len(c) for c in chunk(text, 4)]
""",
        "text/__init__.py": """\
from .chunking import chunk

__all__ = ["chunk"]
""",
        "text/chunking.py": """\
def chunk(text: str, size: int) -> list[str]:
    if size <= 0:
        raise ValueError("size must be > 0")
    return [text[i : i + size] for i in range(0, len(text), size)]
""",
        "cli.py": """\
from . import __version__


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    print(f"ragkit {__version__}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
""",
        "__main__.py": """\
from .cli import main

raise SystemExit(main())
""",
    }


def write_package(root: Path) -> Path:
    pkg = Path(root) / "ragkit"
    for rel, source in _sources().items():
        target = pkg / rel
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        target.write_text(source, encoding="utf-8")
    return pkg

Import machinery: load, locate, shadow, discover★★★ · ex04_import_machinery

Problem

  1. import_from_path(path, module_name) -> ModuleType

    • load a .py file that is not on sys.path (a user-supplied tool, a config script) via importlib.util.spec_from_file_location + module_from_spec
    • register it in sys.modules[module_name] BEFORE executing it (dataclasses, pickling and recursive imports look the module up there), then execute it
    • if executing raises: remove it from sys.modules again and re-raise
    • missing file -> FileNotFoundError

  2. find_origin(name, path=None) -> str | None

    • which entry of path (default sys.path) the TOP-LEVEL module name would be imported from - WITHOUT importing/executing it (importlib.machinery.PathFinder)
    • the first entry that has it wins (that's shadowing!); not found -> None
    • built-in modules (sys.builtin_module_names, e.g. "sys") -> "built-in"

  3. shadowing_modules(directory, extra=()) -> list[str]

    • names of modules in directory that would shadow a standard-library module (sys.stdlib_module_names) or a name in extra (e.g. {"openai"}) if the directory came first on sys.path: "random.py", or a package dir "json/" WITH init.py
    • a directory WITHOUT init.py does not count: namespace packages lose to any regular module/package found later on the path
    • sorted, without duplicates

  4. discover_tools(package_name) -> dict[str, Callable[..., Any]]

    • plugin registry for an agent: import the package, iterate its submodules with pkgutil.iter_modules(pkg.path), skip names starting with "_", import each (importlib.import_module with the full dotted name)
    • a submodule that defines a callable TOOL contributes {getattr(mod, "NAME", submodule_name): TOOL}; modules without TOOL are ignored
    • two modules registering the same NAME -> ValueError

Interviewers look for

  • sys.path order: script dir / cwd first, then PYTHONPATH, stdlib, site-packages -> a local json.py/openai.py silently shadows the real one.
  • sys.modules is the import cache: a module executes once per process; registering before exec is what makes circular imports partially work.
  • find_spec vs import: locating doesn't run code.
  • Plugin discovery with pkgutil / entry points (importlib.metadata.entry_points).

import importlib
import importlib.machinery
import importlib.util
import pkgutil
import sys
from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Sequence
from pathlib import Path
from types import ModuleType
from typing import Any


def import_from_path(path: str | Path, module_name: str) -> ModuleType:
    path = Path(path)
    if not path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(path)
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(module_name, path)
    if spec is None or spec.loader is None:
        raise ImportError(f"cannot load {path}")
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys.modules[module_name] = module
    try:
        spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    except BaseException:
        sys.modules.pop(module_name, None)
        raise
    return module


def find_origin(name: str, path: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> str | None:
    if name in sys.builtin_module_names:
        return "built-in"
    for entry in sys.path if path is None else path:
        if importlib.machinery.PathFinder.find_spec(name, [entry]) is not None:
            return entry
    return None


def shadowing_modules(directory: str | Path, extra: Iterable[str] = ()) -> list[str]:
    protected = set(sys.stdlib_module_names) | set(extra)
    found: set[str] = set()
    for p in Path(directory).iterdir():
        if p.is_file() and p.suffix == ".py":
            name = p.stem
        elif p.is_dir() and (p / "__init__.py").is_file():
            name = p.name
        else:
            continue
        if name in protected:
            found.add(name)
    return sorted(found)


def discover_tools(package_name: str) -> dict[str, Callable[..., Any]]:
    pkg = importlib.import_module(package_name)
    tools: dict[str, Callable[..., Any]] = {}
    for info in pkgutil.iter_modules(pkg.__path__):
        if info.name.startswith("_"):
            continue
        mod = importlib.import_module(f"{package_name}.{info.name}")
        tool = getattr(mod, "TOOL", None)
        if not callable(tool):
            continue
        name = getattr(mod, "NAME", info.name)
        if name in tools:
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate tool name {name!r} in {mod.__name__}")
        tools[name] = tool
    return tools

Python Type Hints

Typed chat messages (TypedDict + Literal)★☆☆ · ex01_chat_messages

type_hints.functions, type_hints.returns, type_hints.optional, type_hints.collections

Problem

The types are given: Role (a Literal) and ChatMessage (a TypedDict) - the exact shape chat-completion APIs use. Type hints are NOT checked at runtime, so data coming from JSON/HTTP still has to be validated by code - ideally derived from the same types, so there is one source of truth.

  1. make_message(role, content, name=None) -> ChatMessage

    • role must be one of the Literal's values - read them with typing.get_args(Role), don't repeat the strings -> ValueError otherwise
    • content must be a str -> TypeError otherwise
    • the "name" key is present only when name is not None

  2. validate_messages(raw: list[dict[str, object]]) -> list[ChatMessage]

    • every item must be a dict with all required keys of ChatMessage (ChatMessage.required_keys), no keys outside required + optional (optional_keys), a valid role, str content, and str name if present
    • any problem -> ValueError whose message starts with f"message {index}: "
    • returns NEW dicts (mutating the result must not change the input)

  3. tokens_by_role(messages, count=len) -> dict[Role, int]

    • sum count(content) per role; roles that don't occur are absent

  4. last_message(messages, role="user") -> ChatMessage | None

    • the last message with that role, or None

Interviewers look for

  • Annotations are metadata: Python never enforces them; mypy/pyright do, statically.
  • TypedDict = typed dict shape (zero runtime cost, JSON-friendly) vs dataclass / pydantic model (real classes, pydantic validates at runtime).
  • X | None (Optional) means "may be None" - not "the argument is optional".
  • Literal for closed sets of strings (roles, finish reasons) + get_args() to reuse them.

Work in exercises/py/14_type_hints/ex01_chat_messages.py (or copy the starter code into any scratch file).

from typing import Literal, NotRequired, TypedDict, get_args
Role = Literal['system', 'user', 'assistant', 'tool']

class ChatMessage(TypedDict):
    role: Role
    content: str
    name: NotRequired[str]

def make_message(role: Role, content: str, name: str | None=None) -> ChatMessage:
    raise NotImplementedError

def validate_messages(raw: list[dict[str, object]]) -> list[ChatMessage]:
    raise NotImplementedError

def tokens_by_role(messages: Sequence[ChatMessage], count: Callable[[str], int]=len) -> dict[Role, int]:
    raise NotImplementedError

def last_message(messages: Sequence[ChatMessage], role: Role='user') -> ChatMessage | None:
    raise NotImplementedError

from collections.abc import Callable, Sequence
from typing import Literal, NotRequired, TypedDict, get_args

Role = Literal["system", "user", "assistant", "tool"]


class ChatMessage(TypedDict):
    role: Role
    content: str
    name: NotRequired[str]


def make_message(role: Role, content: str, name: str | None = None) -> ChatMessage:
    if role not in get_args(Role):
        raise ValueError(f"invalid role {role!r}; expected one of {get_args(Role)}")
    if not isinstance(content, str):
        raise TypeError(f"content must be str, got {type(content).__name__}")
    msg: ChatMessage = {"role": role, "content": content}
    if name is not None:
        msg["name"] = name
    return msg


def validate_messages(raw: list[dict[str, object]]) -> list[ChatMessage]:
    allowed = ChatMessage.__required_keys__ | ChatMessage.__optional_keys__
    out: list[ChatMessage] = []
    for i, item in enumerate(raw):
        if not isinstance(item, dict):
            raise ValueError(f"message {i}: expected an object, got {type(item).__name__}")
        missing = ChatMessage.__required_keys__ - item.keys()
        extra = item.keys() - allowed
        if missing or extra:
            raise ValueError(f"message {i}: missing {sorted(missing)}, unknown {sorted(extra)}")
        name = item.get("name")
        if "name" in item and not isinstance(name, str):
            raise ValueError(f"message {i}: name must be a string")
        try:
            out.append(make_message(item["role"], item["content"], name))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        except (ValueError, TypeError) as e:
            raise ValueError(f"message {i}: {e}") from e
    return out


def tokens_by_role(messages: Sequence[ChatMessage], count: Callable[[str], int] = len) -> dict[Role, int]:
    totals: dict[Role, int] = {}
    for m in messages:
        totals[m["role"]] = totals.get(m["role"], 0) + count(m["content"])
    return totals


def last_message(messages: Sequence[ChatMessage], role: Role = "user") -> ChatMessage | None:
    for m in reversed(messages):
        if m["role"] == role:
            return m
    return None

A mini runtime type checker (pydantic-lite)★★★ · ex02_runtime_type_checker

type_hints.any_vs_object, type_hints.literal, type_hints.aliases, type_hints.typeddict, type_hints.callable, type_hints.functions, type_hints.generics

Problem

LLM "structured output" must be validated against the type you expect. Build the core of what pydantic/typeguard/beartype do, using typing.get_origin / get_args / get_type_hints.

  1. check_type(value, tp) -> bool tp value is accepted when ---------------------------------- ------------------------------------------- Any, object always None (or type(None)) value is None float int or float (PEP 484 numeric promotion) a plain class (int, str, MyClass) isinstance(value, tp) X | Y, Union[X, Y], Optional[X] it matches any member Literal[a, b] == one of them AND same type (True != 1 here) list[X], set[X], frozenset[X] right container type, every item matches X tuple[X, Y] / tuple[X, ...] / tuple[()] fixed length & per-position / any length dict[K, V] a dict whose keys match K and values match V Sequence[X] / Mapping[K, V] isinstance of the abc + items checked (a str IS a Sequence[str] - that's Python) Iterable[X], Iterator[X] isinstance of the abc only (don't consume!) Callable[..., R] callable(value) (signatures aren't checked) a TypedDict class a dict with all required keys, no unknown keys, every present value matches its hint Annotated[X, ...] check against X a type Alias = ... alias (3.12) check against Alias.value bare list / dict / tuple isinstance only anything else (e.g. a TypeVar) raise TypeError("unsupported type ...")

  2. @validate_call - decorator

    • on every call, bind the arguments (inspect.signature), and check each annotated parameter with check_type (*args: each element, **kwargs: each value) -> TypeError naming the parameter if it doesn't match
    • check the return value against the return annotation -> TypeError
    • resolve annotations with typing.get_type_hints (so string annotations work); resolve them once, lazily on the first call is fine
    • keep the function's metadata (functools.wraps)

Interviewers look for

  • get_origin/get_args - how list[int], int | None and Literal[...] look at runtime.
  • Any vs object: both accept everything here, but statically Any switches checking OFF, object allows almost no operations without narrowing.
  • What can't be checked at runtime: generators/iterators (consuming them), Callable signatures, TypeVars - and why static checking is still needed.
  • bool is a subclass of int - a classic validation bug (Literal handles it).

)

F = TypeVar("F", bound=Callable[..., Any])


def _check_typeddict(value: object, td: Any) -> bool:
    if not isinstance(value, dict):
        return False
    hints = get_type_hints(td)
    required: frozenset[str] = td.__required_keys__
    if not required <= value.keys() or not value.keys() <= hints.keys():
        return False
    return all(check_type(v, hints[k]) for k, v in value.items())


def check_type(value: object, tp: Any) -> bool:
    if tp is Any or tp is object:
        return True
    if tp is None or tp is type(None):
        return value is None
    if isinstance(tp, TypeAliasType):
        return check_type(value, tp.__value__)
    if is_typeddict(tp):
        return _check_typeddict(value, tp)
    if tp is float:
        return isinstance(value, (int, float))

    origin, args = get_origin(tp), get_args(tp)
    if origin is None:
        if isinstance(tp, type):
            return isinstance(value, tp)
        raise TypeError(f"unsupported type {tp!r}")

    if origin is Annotated:
        return check_type(value, args[0])
    if origin is Union or origin is types.UnionType:
        return any(check_type(value, a) for a in args)
    if origin is Literal:
        return any(value == a and type(value) is type(a) for a in args)
    if origin is cabc.Callable:
        return callable(value)
    if origin is tuple:
        if not isinstance(value, tuple):
            return False
        if len(args) == 2 and args[1] is Ellipsis:
            return all(check_type(v, args[0]) for v in value)
        if args == ((),):  # tuple[()] on older reprs
            return value == ()
        return len(value) == len(args) and all(map(check_type, value, args))
    if origin in (dict, cabc.Mapping, cabc.MutableMapping):
        if not isinstance(value, origin):
            return False
        k_tp, v_tp = args or (Any, Any)
        return all(check_type(k, k_tp) and check_type(v, v_tp) for k, v in value.items())
    if origin in (list, set, frozenset, cabc.Sequence, cabc.MutableSequence, cabc.Set):
        if not isinstance(value, origin):
            return False
        item_tp = args[0] if args else Any
        return all(check_type(v, item_tp) for v in value)
    if isinstance(origin, type):  # Iterable, Iterator, type[...], user generics...
        return isinstance(value, origin)
    raise TypeError(f"unsupported type {tp!r}")


def validate_call(fn: F) -> F:
    sig = inspect.signature(fn)
    hints: dict[str, Any] | None = None

    @functools.wraps(fn)
    def wrapper(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        nonlocal hints
        if hints is None:
            hints = get_type_hints(fn)
        bound = sig.bind(*args, **kwargs)
        for name, value in bound.arguments.items():
            if name not in hints:
                continue
            kind = sig.parameters[name].kind
            if kind is inspect.Parameter.VAR_POSITIONAL:
                values = list(value)
            elif kind is inspect.Parameter.VAR_KEYWORD:
                values = list(value.values())
            else:
                values = [value]
            if not all(check_type(v, hints[name]) for v in values):
                raise TypeError(f"argument {name!r}={value!r} is not {hints[name]!r}")
        result = fn(*args, **kwargs)
        if "return" in hints and not check_type(result, hints["return"]):
            raise TypeError(f"return value {result!r} is not {hints['return']!r}")
        return result

    return wrapper  # type: ignore[return-value]

Generic TTL cache, Result type, bounded TypeVar★★☆ · ex03_generics

type_hints.protocol, type_hints.static_checking

Problem

Uses Python 3.12 generic syntax (PEP 695): class C[K, V], def f[T](...), type Alias[T] = .... The Ok/Err/Result types and the HasScore protocol are given.

  1. class TTLCache[K, V] - cache for embeddings / LLM responses TTLCache(ttl: float, *, max_size: int = 128, clock=time.monotonic)

    • ttl <= 0 or max_size < 1 -> ValueError
    • set(key, value): store with expiry clock() + ttl; re-setting a key refreshes it
    • get(key) -> V | None: None if missing or expired (expired entries are removed)
    • get_or_set(key, factory: Callable[[], V]) -> V: cached value, or call factory once, store and return its result
    • len(cache): number of NOT expired entries
    • when a set() would exceed max_size, drop expired entries first, then the oldest-inserted ones

  2. try_callT -> Result[T] Ok(fn()) or Err(exception) for any Exception (BaseException propagates)

  3. unwrap_orT -> T

  4. collectT -> Result[list[T]] Ok(list of values) if all are Ok, otherwise the FIRST Err (stop iterating there)

  5. top_kS: HasScore -> list[S] the k items with the highest .score, highest first, ties keep input order; k < 0 -> ValueError. The return type is list[S] - the caller's own type, not list[HasScore] - that's what the bound TypeVar buys you (mypy checks this).

Interviewers look for

  • TypeVar vs Union: def first[T](xs: list[T]) -> T links input and output types; list[int | str] -> int | str loses that.
  • Bounded TypeVars (S: HasScore) vs constrained (T: (str, bytes)).
  • Generic classes: the type parameters exist for the type checker; at runtime TTLCache[str, int] is the same class (type erasure), visible only via type_params / orig_class / get_args.
  • Result/Either types as an alternative to exceptions for batch pipelines.

Work in exercises/py/14_type_hints/ex03_generics.py (or copy the starter code into any scratch file).

import time
from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Protocol

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Ok[T]:
    value: T

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Err:
    error: Exception
type Result[T] = Ok[T] | Err

class HasScore(Protocol):

    @property
    def score(self) -> float:
        ...

class TTLCache[K, V]:

    def __init__(self, ttl: float, *, max_size: int=128, clock: Callable[[], float]=time.monotonic) -> None:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def set(self, key: K, value: V) -> None:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def get(self, key: K) -> V | None:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def get_or_set(self, key: K, factory: Callable[[], V]) -> V:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        raise NotImplementedError

def try_call[T](fn: Callable[[], T]) -> Result[T]:
    raise NotImplementedError

def unwrap_or[T](result: Result[T], default: T) -> T:
    raise NotImplementedError

def collect[T](results: Iterable[Result[T]]) -> Result[list[T]]:
    raise NotImplementedError

def top_k[S: HasScore](items: Iterable[S], k: int) -> list[S]:
    raise NotImplementedError

import time
from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Protocol

__stub_keep__ = ["Ok", "Err", "HasScore"]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Ok[T]:
    value: T


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Err:
    error: Exception


type Result[T] = Ok[T] | Err


class HasScore(Protocol):
    @property
    def score(self) -> float: ...


class TTLCache[K, V]:
    def __init__(
        self, ttl: float, *, max_size: int = 128, clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic
    ) -> None:
        if ttl <= 0:
            raise ValueError("ttl must be > 0")
        if max_size < 1:
            raise ValueError("max_size must be >= 1")
        self.ttl = ttl
        self.max_size = max_size
        self._clock = clock
        self._data: dict[K, tuple[float, V]] = {}  # insertion-ordered: oldest first

    def _purge(self) -> None:
        now = self._clock()
        for key in [k for k, (exp, _) in self._data.items() if exp <= now]:
            del self._data[key]

    def set(self, key: K, value: V) -> None:
        self._data.pop(key, None)  # re-insert at the end
        if len(self._data) >= self.max_size:
            self._purge()
        while len(self._data) >= self.max_size:
            del self._data[next(iter(self._data))]
        self._data[key] = (self._clock() + self.ttl, value)

    def get(self, key: K) -> V | None:
        entry = self._data.get(key)
        if entry is None:
            return None
        expires, value = entry
        if expires <= self._clock():
            del self._data[key]
            return None
        return value

    def get_or_set(self, key: K, factory: Callable[[], V]) -> V:
        entry = self._data.get(key)
        if entry is not None and entry[0] > self._clock():
            return entry[1]
        value = factory()
        self.set(key, value)
        return value

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        self._purge()
        return len(self._data)


def try_call[T](fn: Callable[[], T]) -> Result[T]:
    try:
        return Ok(fn())
    except Exception as e:
        return Err(e)


def unwrap_or[T](result: Result[T], default: T) -> T:
    return result.value if isinstance(result, Ok) else default


def collect[T](results: Iterable[Result[T]]) -> Result[list[T]]:
    values: list[T] = []
    for r in results:
        if isinstance(r, Err):
            return r
        values.append(r.value)
    return Ok(values)


def top_k[S: HasScore](items: Iterable[S], k: int) -> list[S]:
    if k < 0:
        raise ValueError("k must be >= 0")
    return sorted(items, key=lambda it: it.score, reverse=True)[:k]  # sorted is stable
How did it go?
Structural typing: an Embedder Protocol★★☆ · ex04_embedder_protocol

type_hints.any_vs_object, type_hints.static_checking

Problem

Your RAG code should work with OpenAI, a local sentence-transformers model, or a fake in tests - without them sharing a base class. Embedder (a runtime_checkable Protocol) is given.

  1. class HashingEmbedder(dim=8) - a deterministic, dependency-free embedder

    • does NOT inherit from Embedder - it satisfies it structurally
    • dim < 1 -> ValueError; attribute .dim
    • embed(texts) -> one vector per text: for each lower-cased whitespace token, index = int(hashlib.sha256(token.encode()).hexdigest(), 16) % dim, add 1.0 there; then L2-normalize (an all-zero vector, e.g. for "", stays all zeros) (Python's hash() is salted per process - why can't you use it here?)

  2. class CachingEmbedder(inner: Embedder)

    • .dim is inner's dim; .calls counts calls to inner.embed
    • embed(texts): look up each text in a cache; call inner.embed AT MOST ONCE per embed() call, with only the uncached texts, de-duplicated, in first-seen order; return vectors in the order of texts. No call at all if everything is cached.

  3. embed_in_batches(embedder: Embedder, texts, batch_size=32) -> list[list[float]]

    • isinstance(embedder, Embedder) must hold, else TypeError (runtime_checkable)
    • batch_size < 1 -> ValueError
    • calls embedder.embed on consecutive slices of at most batch_size texts
    • every returned vector must have length embedder.dim -> ValueError otherwise (a runtime Protocol check only sees that the members EXIST)

  4. cosine(a, b) -> float cosine similarity; 0.0 if either vector is all zeros; different lengths -> ValueError

Interviewers look for

  • Protocol (structural, "duck typing the type checker understands") vs ABC (nominal, must inherit/register). Protocols fit third-party classes you can't modify.
  • @runtime_checkable isinstance() checks only that the attributes exist - not signatures or return types.
  • Sequence[str] for read-only inputs (accepts list, tuple) vs list[str] for outputs.

Work in exercises/py/14_type_hints/ex04_embedder_protocol.py (or copy the starter code into any scratch file).

import hashlib
import math
from collections.abc import Sequence
from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable

@runtime_checkable
class Embedder(Protocol):
    dim: int

    def embed(self, texts: Sequence[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
        ...

class HashingEmbedder:

    def __init__(self, dim: int=8) -> None:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def embed(self, texts: Sequence[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
        raise NotImplementedError

class CachingEmbedder:

    def __init__(self, inner: Embedder) -> None:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def embed(self, texts: Sequence[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
        raise NotImplementedError

def embed_in_batches(embedder: Embedder, texts: Sequence[str], batch_size: int=32) -> list[list[float]]:
    raise NotImplementedError

def cosine(a: Sequence[float], b: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    raise NotImplementedError

import hashlib
import math
from collections.abc import Sequence
from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable

__stub_keep__ = ["Embedder"]


@runtime_checkable
class Embedder(Protocol):
    dim: int

    def embed(self, texts: Sequence[str]) -> list[list[float]]: ...


class HashingEmbedder:
    def __init__(self, dim: int = 8) -> None:
        if dim < 1:
            raise ValueError("dim must be >= 1")
        self.dim = dim

    def embed(self, texts: Sequence[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
        out: list[list[float]] = []
        for text in texts:
            vec = [0.0] * self.dim
            for token in text.lower().split():
                vec[int(hashlib.sha256(token.encode()).hexdigest(), 16) % self.dim] += 1.0
            norm = math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in vec))
            out.append([x / norm for x in vec] if norm else vec)
        return out


class CachingEmbedder:
    def __init__(self, inner: Embedder) -> None:
        self.inner = inner
        self.dim = inner.dim
        self.calls = 0
        self._cache: dict[str, list[float]] = {}

    def embed(self, texts: Sequence[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
        missing = list(dict.fromkeys(t for t in texts if t not in self._cache))
        if missing:
            self.calls += 1
            for text, vec in zip(missing, self.inner.embed(missing), strict=True):
                self._cache[text] = vec
        return [self._cache[t] for t in texts]


def embed_in_batches(embedder: Embedder, texts: Sequence[str], batch_size: int = 32) -> list[list[float]]:
    if not isinstance(embedder, Embedder):
        raise TypeError(f"{type(embedder).__name__} does not implement Embedder")
    if batch_size < 1:
        raise ValueError("batch_size must be >= 1")
    vectors: list[list[float]] = []
    for start in range(0, len(texts), batch_size):
        batch = embedder.embed(texts[start : start + batch_size])
        if any(len(v) != embedder.dim for v in batch):
            raise ValueError(f"embedder returned vectors that are not of dim {embedder.dim}")
        vectors.extend(batch)
    return vectors


def cosine(a: Sequence[float], b: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    if len(a) != len(b):
        raise ValueError("vectors must have the same length")
    na = math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in a))
    nb = math.sqrt(sum(y * y for y in b))
    if not na or not nb:
        return 0.0
    return sum(x * y for x, y in zip(a, b, strict=True)) / (na * nb)

Typing decorators & overloads (mypy --strict)★★★ · ex05_typed_decorators

type_hints.literal, type_hints.static_checking, type_hints.mypy_pyright, type_hints.aliases

Problem

This module must pass mypy --strict (the tests run it) - including your code.

  1. retry(*, attempts=3, exceptions=(Exception,), base_delay=0.1, sleep=time.sleep) -> a decorator that keeps the decorated function's EXACT signature for type checkers

    • uses ParamSpec (PEP 695 syntax: def retry[**P, R](...)) so that after @retry(attempts=2) def ask(prompt: str, temperature: float = 0.0) -> str: ... mypy still knows ask(prompt: str, temperature: float = 0.0) -> str and rejects ask(123). (Typing the decorator as Callable[..., Any] would silently accept it.)
    • attempts < 1 -> ValueError when retry(...) is called
    • calls the function; on one of exceptions sleeps base_delay * 2**k and retries; after the last attempt re-raises the last exception; other exceptions propagate
    • functools.wraps

  2. get_setting(key) with @overload: get_setting("temperature") -> float, get_setting("max_tokens") -> int, get_setting("model") -> str ; values come from the SETTINGS dict (given); any other key -> KeyError. mypy must infer the precise return type per literal. (The three @overload signatures are given; in real code their bodies are just .... Only the final, undecorated get_setting is implemented.)

  3. composeA, B, C -> Callable[[A], C] compose(f, g)(x) == g(f(x))

  4. pipelineT -> Callable[[T], T] applies the steps left to right; no steps -> identity

Interviewers look for

  • Callable[[Args], R] vs Callable[..., R]; ParamSpec / Concatenate for decorators (the most common place where types get lost in real codebases).
  • @overload + Literal for APIs whose return type depends on an argument value (open(mode="rb") returns BinaryIO - same idea).
  • mypy vs pyright: both implement the typing spec; pyright is faster and stricter about inference, mypy has plugins (pydantic, django). Run one in CI with --strict on new code.

Work in exercises/py/14_type_hints/ex05_typed_decorators.py (or copy the starter code into any scratch file).

import time
from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import Final, Literal, overload
SETTINGS: Final[dict[str, float | int | str]] = {'temperature': 0.2, 'max_tokens': 1024, 'model': 'gpt-4o-mini'}
type SettingKey = Literal['temperature', 'max_tokens', 'model']

def retry[**P, R](*, attempts: int=3, exceptions: tuple[type[Exception], ...]=(Exception,), base_delay: float=0.1, sleep: Callable[[float], object]=time.sleep) -> Callable[[Callable[P, R]], Callable[P, R]]:
    raise NotImplementedError

@overload
def get_setting(key: Literal['temperature']) -> float:
    raise NotImplementedError

@overload
def get_setting(key: Literal['max_tokens']) -> int:
    raise NotImplementedError

@overload
def get_setting(key: Literal['model']) -> str:
    raise NotImplementedError

def get_setting(key: SettingKey) -> float | int | str:
    raise NotImplementedError

def compose[A, B, C](f: Callable[[A], B], g: Callable[[B], C]) -> Callable[[A], C]:
    raise NotImplementedError

def pipeline[T](*steps: Callable[[T], T]) -> Callable[[T], T]:
    raise NotImplementedError

import functools
import time
from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import Final, Literal, overload

SETTINGS: Final[dict[str, float | int | str]] = {
    "temperature": 0.2,
    "max_tokens": 1024,
    "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
}

type SettingKey = Literal["temperature", "max_tokens", "model"]


def retry[**P, R](
    *,
    attempts: int = 3,
    exceptions: tuple[type[Exception], ...] = (Exception,),
    base_delay: float = 0.1,
    sleep: Callable[[float], object] = time.sleep,
) -> Callable[[Callable[P, R]], Callable[P, R]]:
    if attempts < 1:
        raise ValueError("attempts must be >= 1")

    def decorator(fn: Callable[P, R]) -> Callable[P, R]:
        @functools.wraps(fn)
        def wrapper(*args: P.args, **kwargs: P.kwargs) -> R:
            for attempt in range(attempts):
                try:
                    return fn(*args, **kwargs)
                except exceptions:
                    if attempt == attempts - 1:
                        raise
                    sleep(base_delay * 2**attempt)
            raise AssertionError("unreachable")  # pragma: no cover

        return wrapper

    return decorator


@overload
def get_setting(key: Literal["temperature"]) -> float: ...
@overload
def get_setting(key: Literal["max_tokens"]) -> int: ...
@overload
def get_setting(key: Literal["model"]) -> str: ...
def get_setting(key: SettingKey) -> float | int | str:
    if key not in SETTINGS:
        raise KeyError(key)
    value: float | int | str = SETTINGS[key]
    return value


def compose[A, B, C](f: Callable[[A], B], g: Callable[[B], C]) -> Callable[[A], C]:
    def composed(x: A) -> C:
        return g(f(x))

    return composed


def pipeline[T](*steps: Callable[[T], T]) -> Callable[[T], T]:
    def run(x: T) -> T:
        for step in steps:
            x = step(x)
        return x

    return run

Pydantic

Chat-completion messages★☆☆ · ex01_chat_messages

pydantic.custom_validators, pydantic.model_validator, pydantic.validation

Problem

The FIELDS of the models below are given (read them - they are part of the spec). Your job is the validation logic and two small methods.

FunctionCall(name, arguments) arguments is the raw JSON string the LLM produced ToolCall(id, type="function", function: FunctionCall) Message(role, content=None, name=None, tool_calls=None, tool_call_id=None) Conversation(messages: list[Message])

  1. Message.normalise_role - field_validator("role", mode="before")

    • if the raw value is a str: strip whitespace and lowercase it (" User " -> "user")
    • anything else is returned unchanged (so the Literal type rejects it normally)

  2. Message.clean_content - field_validator("content") (runs AFTER str validation)

    • strip surrounding whitespace; a whitespace-only / empty string becomes None

  3. Message.check_shape - model_validator(mode="after"), raise ValueError on:

    • role "tool" without tool_call_id, or without content
    • tool_calls on any role other than "assistant"
    • tool_call_id on any role other than "tool"
    • role "assistant" with neither content nor tool_calls
    • role "system"/"user" without content returns self when valid

  4. ToolCall.parsed_arguments() -> dict

    • json.loads(function.arguments); must decode to a dict, else ValueError (json.JSONDecodeError is already a ValueError subclass - let it propagate)

  5. Conversation.check_order - model_validator(mode="after")

    • at least one message (ValueError otherwise)
    • a "system" message is only allowed at index 0
    • every "tool" message must answer a tool call id issued by an EARLIER assistant message in the conversation

  6. Conversation.last_assistant_text() -> str | None

    • content of the last assistant message that has content, else None

All violations must surface as pydantic.ValidationError when constructing the model (raising ValueError inside a validator is what makes pydantic wrap it).

Interviewers look for

  • mode="before" sees the RAW input (could be anything); the default "after" sees the already type-validated value - choose based on whether you need to pre-process.
  • Required vs optional: x: str | None WITHOUT a default is still REQUIRED in pydantic v2; it only becomes optional with = None.
  • Cross-field rules belong in a model_validator(mode="after"), where all fields are typed.
  • Validators raise ValueError/AssertionError -> pydantic collects them into ValidationError; any other exception type escapes un-wrapped (a classic bug).
  • Nested models validate recursively: errors carry a loc path like ('messages', 2, 'role').

Work in exercises/py/15_pydantic/ex01_chat_messages.py (or copy the starter code into any scratch file).

import json
from typing import Any, Literal, Self
from pydantic import BaseModel, field_validator, model_validator
Role = Literal['system', 'user', 'assistant', 'tool']

class FunctionCall(BaseModel):
    name: str
    arguments: str

class ToolCall(BaseModel):
    id: str
    type: Literal['function'] = 'function'
    function: FunctionCall

    def parsed_arguments(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        raise NotImplementedError

class Message(BaseModel):
    role: Role
    content: str | None = None
    name: str | None = None
    tool_calls: list[ToolCall] | None = None
    tool_call_id: str | None = None

    @field_validator('role', mode='before')
    @classmethod
    def normalise_role(cls, value: Any) -> Any:
        raise NotImplementedError

    @field_validator('content')
    @classmethod
    def clean_content(cls, value: str | None) -> str | None:
        raise NotImplementedError

    @model_validator(mode='after')
    def check_shape(self) -> Self:
        raise NotImplementedError

class Conversation(BaseModel):
    messages: list[Message]

    @model_validator(mode='after')
    def check_order(self) -> Self:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def last_assistant_text(self) -> str | None:
        raise NotImplementedError

import json
from typing import Any, Literal, Self

from pydantic import BaseModel, field_validator, model_validator

Role = Literal["system", "user", "assistant", "tool"]


class FunctionCall(BaseModel):
    name: str
    arguments: str  # JSON-encoded string, exactly as the LLM emitted it


class ToolCall(BaseModel):
    id: str
    type: Literal["function"] = "function"
    function: FunctionCall

    def parsed_arguments(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        args = json.loads(self.function.arguments)
        if not isinstance(args, dict):
            raise ValueError(f"tool arguments must be a JSON object, got {type(args).__name__}")
        return args


class Message(BaseModel):
    role: Role
    content: str | None = None
    name: str | None = None
    tool_calls: list[ToolCall] | None = None
    tool_call_id: str | None = None

    @field_validator("role", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def normalise_role(cls, value: Any) -> Any:
        if isinstance(value, str):
            return value.strip().lower()
        return value

    @field_validator("content")
    @classmethod
    def clean_content(cls, value: str | None) -> str | None:
        if value is None:
            return None
        value = value.strip()
        return value or None

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def check_shape(self) -> Self:
        if self.tool_calls is not None and self.role != "assistant":
            raise ValueError("only assistant messages may contain tool_calls")
        if self.tool_call_id is not None and self.role != "tool":
            raise ValueError("only tool messages may have a tool_call_id")
        match self.role:
            case "tool":
                if self.tool_call_id is None or self.content is None:
                    raise ValueError("tool messages need tool_call_id and content")
            case "assistant":
                if self.content is None and not self.tool_calls:
                    raise ValueError("assistant message needs content or tool_calls")
            case _:
                if self.content is None:
                    raise ValueError(f"{self.role} message needs content")
        return self


class Conversation(BaseModel):
    messages: list[Message]

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def check_order(self) -> Self:
        if not self.messages:
            raise ValueError("conversation needs at least one message")
        issued: set[str] = set()
        for i, msg in enumerate(self.messages):
            if msg.role == "system" and i != 0:
                raise ValueError(f"system message only allowed first (found at {i})")
            if msg.role == "assistant" and msg.tool_calls:
                issued.update(tc.id for tc in msg.tool_calls)
            if msg.role == "tool" and msg.tool_call_id not in issued:
                raise ValueError(f"tool message {i} answers unknown call {msg.tool_call_id!r}")
        return self

    def last_assistant_text(self) -> str | None:
        for msg in reversed(self.messages):
            if msg.role == "assistant" and msg.content is not None:
                return msg.content
        return None

camelCase API payloads: aliases, model_dump, round-trips★☆☆ · ex02_api_serialization

pydantic.api_validation

Problem

An embedding service speaks camelCase JSON (jobId, modelName, createdAt...), our Python code uses snake_case. The fields + model_config of EmbeddingJob and JobUpdate are given; read the config (alias_generator=to_camel, validate_by_name).

Implement on EmbeddingJob:

  1. num_inputs - a @computed_field property: len(input_texts). It must appear in dumps.

  2. serialize_created_at - @field_serializer("created_at", when_used="json")

    • output ISO-8601 in UTC with a trailing "Z", seconds precision: "2024-05-01T12:00:00Z"
    • a naive datetime is assumed to already be UTC; an aware one is converted to UTC
    • (when_used="json": python-mode dumps keep the real datetime object)

  3. to_api(self) -> dict

    • JSON-compatible dict for the HTTP body: camelCase keys, None values omitted, UUID -> str, datetime -> the "Z" string above, includes "numInputs"
    • api_key must NEVER be in the output (it is declared with exclude=True - check that you didn't defeat that)

  4. to_db_row(self) -> dict

    • python-mode dump with snake_case keys, None values KEPT, real UUID/datetime objects

  5. from_api(cls, data) -> EmbeddingJob (classmethod)

    • data may be a dict (already-parsed JSON) -> use model_validate
    • or str/bytes (raw HTTP body) -> use model_validate_json (one fast pass in Rust, no intermediate dict)
    • accepts camelCase or snake_case keys; invalid input -> pydantic.ValidationError

And a function:

  1. patch_body(update: JobUpdate) -> dict
    • body for a PATCH request: camelCase, JSON mode, containing ONLY the fields the caller explicitly set - including fields explicitly set to None (that means "clear it" in our API). Fields left at their default must not be sent.

Interviewers look for

  • exclude_none vs exclude_unset: "not provided" and "explicitly null" are different things in a PATCH. exclude_none would make it impossible to clear a field.
  • mode="python" vs mode="json": python mode keeps UUID/datetime objects; json mode gives only JSON-native types (what you'd put on the wire).
  • by_alias=True on dump; validate_by_name/validate_by_alias on load.
  • model_validate_json(raw) is faster and stricter-per-JSON than json.loads + model_validate.
  • Secrets: Field(exclude=True) / SecretStr so they never leak into logs or payloads.

from datetime import UTC, datetime
from typing import Any, Self
from uuid import UUID

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, SecretStr, computed_field, field_serializer
from pydantic.alias_generators import to_camel

_API_CONFIG = ConfigDict(alias_generator=to_camel, validate_by_name=True, validate_by_alias=True)


class EmbeddingJob(BaseModel):
    model_config = _API_CONFIG

    job_id: UUID
    model_name: str
    input_texts: list[str]
    created_at: datetime
    dimensions: int | None = None
    user_tag: str | None = None
    api_key: SecretStr | None = Field(default=None, exclude=True)

    @computed_field  # type: ignore[prop-decorator]
    @property
    def num_inputs(self) -> int:
        return len(self.input_texts)

    @field_serializer("created_at", when_used="json")
    def serialize_created_at(self, value: datetime) -> str:
        if value.tzinfo is None:
            value = value.replace(tzinfo=UTC)
        return value.astimezone(UTC).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")

    def to_api(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return self.model_dump(mode="json", by_alias=True, exclude_none=True)

    def to_db_row(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return self.model_dump()

    @classmethod
    def from_api(cls, data: dict[str, Any] | str | bytes) -> Self:
        if isinstance(data, (str, bytes)):
            return cls.model_validate_json(data)
        return cls.model_validate(data)


class JobUpdate(BaseModel):
    model_config = _API_CONFIG

    user_tag: str | None = None
    dimensions: int | None = None
    model_name: str | None = None


def patch_body(update: JobUpdate) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return update.model_dump(mode="json", by_alias=True, exclude_unset=True)

Per-provider request schemas (Field constraints)★★☆ · ex03_provider_limits

pydantic.validation, pydantic.json_schema

Problem

An LLM gateway accepts one request shape but every provider has different limits (max output tokens, temperature range, number of stop sequences, seed support). Build the request model per provider.

request_model_for(limits: ProviderLimits) -> type[BaseModel] Model class name: f"{limits.provider.capitalize()}Request" (e.g. "OpenaiRequest"). Config: unknown fields are an ERROR (a typo like "temprature" must not be silently ignored - that's pydantic's default behaviour!).

field type / default rules

model str, REQUIRED whitespace stripped, then min length 1 prompt str, REQUIRED min length 1 max_tokens int, REQUIRED > 0 and <= limits.max_output_tokens; STRICT: "100", 100.0 and True are rejected temperature float = min(1.0, max_temp) 0 <= t <= limits.max_temperature top_p float | None = None 0 < p <= 1 when given stop list[str] = [] at most limits.max_stop_sequences items, each item non-empty; no shared mutable default seed int | None = None ONLY present if limits.supports_seed; otherwise sending seed is an "extra" error

Every field has a short description (it shows up in the JSON schema / API docs). Calling request_model_for twice with equal limits returns the SAME class object (building models is not free - cache them).

Use Field(...) / Annotated constraints - NOT hand-written validators.

Interviewers look for

  • Required vs optional vs nullable: x: int (required), x: int = 0 (optional), x: int | None (required but may be null!), x: int | None = None (optional, nullable).
  • Lax vs strict: by default pydantic coerces "100" -> 100 and True -> 1. For token limits and money, strict=True is often what you want.
  • extra="forbid" for request bodies catches client typos early.
  • Constraints are declarative -> they appear in the JSON schema (maximum, minLength...), hand-written validators don't.
  • create_model() / classes built in a function for config-driven schemas.

class ProviderLimits:

    max_output_tokens: int
    max_temperature: float
    max_stop_sequences: int

@functools.cache

import functools
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Annotated, Any

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, StringConstraints, create_model


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ProviderLimits:
    provider: str
    max_output_tokens: int
    max_temperature: float
    max_stop_sequences: int
    supports_seed: bool = True


@functools.cache
def request_model_for(limits: ProviderLimits) -> type[BaseModel]:
    fields: dict[str, Any] = {
        "model": (
            Annotated[str, StringConstraints(strip_whitespace=True, min_length=1)],
            Field(description="Model identifier, e.g. 'gpt-4o-mini'"),
        ),
        "prompt": (str, Field(min_length=1, description="User prompt")),
        "max_tokens": (
            int,
            Field(
                gt=0,
                le=limits.max_output_tokens,
                strict=True,
                description="Maximum number of tokens to generate",
            ),
        ),
        "temperature": (
            float,
            Field(
                default=min(1.0, limits.max_temperature),
                ge=0,
                le=limits.max_temperature,
                description="Sampling temperature",
            ),
        ),
        "top_p": (float | None, Field(default=None, gt=0, le=1, description="Nucleus sampling")),
        "stop": (
            list[Annotated[str, Field(min_length=1)]],
            Field(
                default_factory=list,
                max_length=limits.max_stop_sequences,
                description="Stop sequences",
            ),
        ),
    }
    if limits.supports_seed:
        fields["seed"] = (int | None, Field(default=None, description="Sampling seed"))
    return create_model(
        f"{limits.provider.capitalize()}Request",
        __config__=ConfigDict(extra="forbid"),
        **fields,
    )

Parsing messy LLM JSON into a model★★☆ · ex04_llm_json_output

pydantic.serialization

Problem

LLMs asked for "JSON only" still reply with things like:

Sure! Here is the triage:
```json
{"category": "bug", "priority": 2, "summary": "Login fails"}
```
Let me know if you need anything else.

TicketTriage and LLMOutputError are given.

  1. extract_json(text) -> str

    • if the text contains a fenced block ( or ```json, any case), search only inside the FIRST fenced block; otherwise search the whole text
    • return the FIRST complete JSON object or array, as the exact substring of the input (prose before it and any trailing text after it are dropped)
    • braces inside prose ("use {name} here") or inside JSON strings must not confuse you -> hint: json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode(s, idx) parses ONE value starting at idx and tells you where it ended
    • nothing parseable -> raise LLMOutputError

  2. parse_llm_output(text, model) -> instance of model

    • extract_json, then validate with model.model_validate_json (pydantic.ValidationError propagates unchanged; LLMOutputError propagates unchanged)
    • generic: must work for any BaseModel subclass

  3. error_feedback(err: ValidationError) -> str A message we send BACK to the LLM so it can fix its output. Exact format:

     Your JSON failed validation with 2 error(s):
 - priority: Input should be less than or equal to 5 (got 9)
 - tags.1: Input should be a valid string (got 3)
 Return ONLY the corrected JSON object.
    • one line per error, in pydantic's order; loc parts joined with "." ; an empty loc is written "(root)"
    • "msg" is pydantic's error message
    • append " (got <repr(input)>)" ONLY when the input is a scalar (str/int/float/bool/ None) AND the error type is not "missing" (missing fields have no useful input)

Interviewers look for

  • Never json.loads LLM output blindly: extraction + schema validation + a structured error you can feed back (that's the core of "structured output" libraries).
  • model_validate_json validates directly from the JSON string (one pass, JSON-mode coercion rules) vs json.loads -> model_validate (two passes, python-mode rules).
  • ValidationError.errors() gives machine-readable dicts: type, loc, msg, input.
  • Don't echo huge inputs back into the prompt (token cost) - only short scalars.

Work in exercises/py/15_pydantic/ex04_llm_json_output.py (or copy the starter code into any scratch file).

import json
import re
from typing import Literal
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, ValidationError

class LLMOutputError(ValueError):
    """The LLM response contains no parseable JSON."""

class TicketTriage(BaseModel):
    category: Literal['bug', 'billing', 'feature_request', 'other']
    priority: int = Field(ge=1, le=5)
    summary: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=200)
    tags: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    needs_human: bool = False

def extract_json(text: str) -> str:
    raise NotImplementedError

def parse_llm_output[M: BaseModel](text: str, model: type[M]) -> M:
    raise NotImplementedError

def error_feedback(err: ValidationError) -> str:
    raise NotImplementedError

import json
import re
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, ValidationError

_FENCE = re.compile(r"```[a-zA-Z]*[ \t]*\n?(.*?)```", re.DOTALL)
_DECODER = json.JSONDecoder()


class LLMOutputError(ValueError):
    """The LLM response contains no parseable JSON."""


class TicketTriage(BaseModel):
    category: Literal["bug", "billing", "feature_request", "other"]
    priority: int = Field(ge=1, le=5)
    summary: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=200)
    tags: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    needs_human: bool = False


def extract_json(text: str) -> str:
    fence = _FENCE.search(text)
    haystack = fence.group(1) if fence else text
    for idx, char in enumerate(haystack):
        if char not in "{[":
            continue
        try:
            _, end = _DECODER.raw_decode(haystack, idx)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        return haystack[idx:end]
    raise LLMOutputError("no JSON object or array found in LLM output")


def parse_llm_output[M: BaseModel](text: str, model: type[M]) -> M:
    return model.model_validate_json(extract_json(text))


def error_feedback(err: ValidationError) -> str:
    errors = err.errors(include_url=False)
    lines = [f"Your JSON failed validation with {len(errors)} error(s):"]
    for e in errors:
        loc = ".".join(str(part) for part in e["loc"]) or "(root)"
        line = f"- {loc}: {e['msg']}"
        value = e.get("input")
        if e["type"] != "missing" and (value is None or isinstance(value, (str, int, float))):
            line += f" (got {value!r})"
        lines.append(line)
    lines.append("Return ONLY the corrected JSON object.")
    return "\n".join(lines)

App configuration with pydantic-settings★★☆ · ex05_app_settings

pydantic.model_validator, pydantic.model_dump

Problem

Configuration for a RAG service, read from environment variables (and optionally a .env file). The fields and model_config of LLMConfig / AppSettings are given - read them: env_prefix="RAG_", env_nested_delimiter="__", so e.g.

RAG_ENV=prod  RAG_API_KEY=sk-...  RAG_LLM__MODEL=gpt-4o  RAG_LLM__TEMPERATURE=0.0
RAG_ALLOWED_MODELS="gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini"

Implement:

  1. AppSettings.split_csv - field_validator("allowed_models", mode="before")

    • a str value is a comma-separated list: split, strip each item, drop empties ("gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini ," -> ["gpt-4o", "gpt-4o-mini"])
    • a str that starts with "[" is a JSON array -> json.loads it
    • any other value (already a list) passes through unchanged (the field is annotated NoDecode so pydantic-settings does NOT try to json-decode it)

  2. AppSettings.check_consistency - model_validator(mode="after"), ValueError if:

    • llm.model is not in allowed_models (any env)
    • env == "prod" and api_key is missing
    • env == "prod" and debug is True

  3. AppSettings.public_dict() -> dict

    • JSON-mode dump safe to log / show on a /config endpoint: secrets come out as "**********" (that's what SecretStr gives in JSON mode), and the password inside database_url (scheme://user:PASSWORD@host/...) is replaced by "***". URLs without a password are unchanged.

  4. get_settings() -> AppSettings

    • build the settings ONCE per process and return the same object afterwards (tests call get_settings.cache_clear() - so use functools.cache / lru_cache)

Interviewers look for

  • Precedence: init kwargs > environment variables > .env file > field defaults.
  • Env values are strings; pydantic coerces "false"/"0"/"no" -> False, "30" -> 30.0. Complex types (list/dict/models) are JSON-decoded unless you opt out (NoDecode).
  • Nested config via env_nested_delimiter, and validating ALL config at startup ("fail fast") instead of crashing on first use deep inside a request.
  • SecretStr: repr/str/JSON dump are masked; .get_secret_value() is explicit.
  • Settings as a cached singleton (dependency injection in FastAPI: Depends(get_settings)), and why tests must clear that cache.

class AppSettings(BaseSettings):

    debug: bool = False

    database_url: str = 'sqlite:///./dev.db'

    @classmethod
    def split_csv(cls, value: Any) -> Any:
        raise NotImplementedError

    @model_validator(mode='after')
    def check_consistency(self) -> Self:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def public_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        raise NotImplementedError

@functools.cache
def get_settings() -> AppSettings:
    raise NotImplementedError

import functools
import json
import re
from typing import Annotated, Any, Literal, Self

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, SecretStr, field_validator, model_validator
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, NoDecode, SettingsConfigDict

_URL_PASSWORD = re.compile(r"(?P<head>://[^:/@]+:)[^@]*(?=@)")


class LLMConfig(BaseModel):
    model: str = "gpt-4o-mini"
    temperature: float = Field(default=0.2, ge=0, le=2)
    timeout_s: float = Field(default=30.0, gt=0)


class AppSettings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(
        env_prefix="RAG_", env_nested_delimiter="__", extra="ignore"
    )

    env: Literal["dev", "staging", "prod"] = "dev"
    debug: bool = False
    api_key: SecretStr | None = None
    database_url: str = "sqlite:///./dev.db"
    allowed_models: Annotated[list[str], NoDecode] = ["gpt-4o-mini"]
    llm: LLMConfig = LLMConfig()

    @field_validator("allowed_models", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def split_csv(cls, value: Any) -> Any:
        if isinstance(value, str):
            if value.lstrip().startswith("["):
                return json.loads(value)
            return [item.strip() for item in value.split(",") if item.strip()]
        return value

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def check_consistency(self) -> Self:
        if self.llm.model not in self.allowed_models:
            raise ValueError(f"llm.model {self.llm.model!r} not in allowed_models")
        if self.env == "prod":
            if self.api_key is None:
                raise ValueError("api_key is required in prod")
            if self.debug:
                raise ValueError("debug must be off in prod")
        return self

    def public_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        data = self.model_dump(mode="json")
        data["database_url"] = _URL_PASSWORD.sub(r"\g<head>***", self.database_url)
        return data


@functools.cache
def get_settings() -> AppSettings:
    return AppSettings()
