LLM tool definitions from models and functions★★★ · ex06_tool_schema

pydantic.model_validate

Problem

Function-calling APIs want each tool as {"type": "function", "function": {"name": ..., "description": ..., "parameters": <JSON schema>}} and many providers reject schemas that contain "$ref"/"$defs" and want every object to forbid unknown keys.

  1. tool_definition(model, name=None, description=None) -> dict

    • name defaults to the class name in snake_case: "GetWeather" -> "get_weather", "SearchKBArticles" -> "search_kb_articles"
    • description defaults to inspect.cleandoc(model.doc), or "" if no docstring
    • parameters = model.model_json_schema(), post-processed:
      • every {"$ref": "#/$defs/X", ...} is replaced by the (processed) definition of X, merged with any sibling keys of the $ref (e.g. a "description"); the top-level "$defs" is removed
      • every "title" KEYWORD is removed - but a property that is literally named "title" (a key inside a "properties" mapping) must survive!
      • every schema with "type": "object" gets "additionalProperties": False unless it already has an "additionalProperties" entry (dict[str, X] fields do)
      • values under "default", "examples", "enum", "const" are data: copy untouched
      • a self-referencing (recursive) model cannot be inlined -> ValueError
    • the input schema must not be mutated in any way that changes later calls

  2. tool_from_function(fn) -> Tool (Tool is a given dataclass)

    • build an args model with pydantic.create_model, one field per parameter: annotation from the signature (Annotated[..., Field(description=...)] metadata kept), parameters with defaults are optional, without defaults required
    • the args model forbids extra keys
    • a parameter without annotation, or *args / **kwargs -> TypeError
    • Tool.name = fn.name, Tool.description = cleaned docstring or ""

  3. invoke_tool(tool, arguments) -> Any

    • arguments: the JSON string from the LLM, or an already-parsed dict
    • validate with the args model (ValidationError propagates), then call tool.fn(**kwargs) with the VALIDATED values - nested BaseModel parameters must arrive as model instances, not dicts (so don't use model_dump() here!)

Interviewers look for

  • Pydantic is the schema source of truth: one model gives validation, JSON schema for the LLM, and typed parsing of the LLM's arguments (what Instructor / OpenAI Agents SDK / LangChain @tool do under the hood).
  • Descriptions on fields are prompt engineering - the model reads them.
  • $ref inlining with cycle detection; distinguishing schema KEYWORDS from property NAMES.
  • LLM-produced arguments are untrusted input: validate before executing.

import inspect
import re
import typing
from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, create_model

_DATA_KEYS = frozenset({"default", "examples", "enum", "const"})


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Tool:
    name: str
    description: str
    args_model: type[BaseModel]
    fn: Callable[..., Any]


def _snake(name: str) -> str:
    name = re.sub(r"([A-Z]+)([A-Z][a-z])", r"\1_\2", name)
    return re.sub(r"([a-z0-9])([A-Z])", r"\1_\2", name).lower()


def _inline(node: Any, defs: dict[str, Any], stack: frozenset[str]) -> Any:
    if isinstance(node, list):
        return [_inline(item, defs, stack) for item in node]
    if not isinstance(node, dict):
        return node
    if "$ref" in node:
        ref_name = node["$ref"].rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
        if ref_name in stack:
            raise ValueError(f"recursive schema via {ref_name!r} cannot be inlined")
        resolved = _inline(defs[ref_name], defs, stack | {ref_name})
        siblings = _inline({k: v for k, v in node.items() if k != "$ref"}, defs, stack)
        return {**resolved, **siblings}
    out: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for key, value in node.items():
        if key in ("$defs", "title"):
            continue
        if key == "properties":
            out[key] = {prop: _inline(sub, defs, stack) for prop, sub in value.items()}
        elif key in _DATA_KEYS:
            out[key] = value
        else:
            out[key] = _inline(value, defs, stack)
    if out.get("type") == "object" and "additionalProperties" not in out:
        out["additionalProperties"] = False
    return out


def tool_definition(
    model: type[BaseModel], name: str | None = None, description: str | None = None
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    schema = model.model_json_schema()
    parameters = _inline(schema, schema.get("$defs", {}), frozenset())
    if description is None:
        description = inspect.cleandoc(model.__doc__) if model.__doc__ else ""
    return {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": name or _snake(model.__name__),
            "description": description,
            "parameters": parameters,
        },
    }


def tool_from_function(fn: Callable[..., Any]) -> Tool:
    hints = typing.get_type_hints(fn, include_extras=True)
    fields: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for param in inspect.signature(fn).parameters.values():
        if param.kind in (param.VAR_POSITIONAL, param.VAR_KEYWORD):
            raise TypeError(f"{fn.__name__}: *args/**kwargs can't be described to an LLM")
        if param.name not in hints:
            raise TypeError(f"{fn.__name__}: parameter {param.name!r} needs a type annotation")
        default = ... if param.default is param.empty else param.default
        fields[param.name] = (hints[param.name], default)
    args_model = create_model(
        f"{fn.__name__}_args", __config__=ConfigDict(extra="forbid"), **fields
    )
    doc = inspect.getdoc(fn) or ""
    return Tool(name=fn.__name__, description=doc, args_model=args_model, fn=fn)


def invoke_tool(tool: Tool, arguments: str | dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
    if isinstance(arguments, str):
        validated = tool.args_model.model_validate_json(arguments)
    else:
        validated = tool.args_model.model_validate(arguments)
    kwargs = {name: getattr(validated, name) for name in type(validated).model_fields}
    return tool.fn(**kwargs)

Agent actions: discriminated unions + repair loop★★★ · ex07_agent_actions

pydantic.models, pydantic.nested

Problem

An agent LLM replies with ONE JSON action per turn, e.g. {"type": "search", "query": "refund policy", "top_k": 3} {"type": "final_answer", "answer": "...", "citations": ["doc-1"]} The action models and AgentOutputError are given.

  1. build_action_adapter(*models) -> pydantic.TypeAdapter

    • a TypeAdapter for a union of the models DISCRIMINATED on the "type" field (Annotated[Union[...], Field(discriminator="type")])
    • no models -> ValueError
    • every model must declare type as a Literal -> otherwise TypeError
    • two models claiming the same tag value -> ValueError (check it yourself, before building the adapter) Effect to observe: an invalid {"type": "search", "top_k": 99} gives ONE error located at ("search", "top_k") instead of one error per union member.

  2. parse_actions(items, adapter) -> (actions, failures)

    • the LLM emitted several actions (parallel tool calls) as already-parsed dicts
    • validate each independently; actions = the valid ones in input order; failures = [(index, ValidationError), ...] for the invalid ones
    • one bad item must not prevent the others from running

  3. next_action(call_llm, messages, adapter, max_attempts=3) -> action

    • call_llm(history: list[dict]) -> str (raw model output)
    • validate the raw text with adapter.validate_json
    • on ValidationError: extend the history with {"role": "assistant", "content": <raw text>} {"role": "user", "content": feedback} where feedback = "Invalid action. Fix these errors and reply with JSON only: " + "; ".join(f"{loc}: {msg}") over err.errors(), loc parts joined by "." ("(root)" if empty) and call the LLM again with the longer history
    • the caller's messages list must NOT be mutated
    • after max_attempts failed attempts raise AgentOutputError(attempts, last_error) chained (raise ... from) to the last ValidationError
    • max_attempts < 1 -> ValueError

Interviewers look for

  • Discriminated (tagged) unions: O(1) dispatch on the tag, precise error locations, and a clean oneOf + discriminator JSON schema; plain unions try members left-to-right and may silently coerce into the wrong one ("smart mode" mitigates but costs).
  • TypeAdapter validates non-BaseModel types (unions, lists, TypedDicts).
  • Self-correction / "reflexion" loop: feed structured validation errors back, bounded by a retry budget; keep the original conversation immutable.

Work in exercises/py/15_pydantic/ex07_agent_actions.py (or copy the starter code into any scratch file).

        self.last_error = last_error

    raise NotImplementedError

    raise NotImplementedError

    raise NotImplementedError

import typing
from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import Annotated, Any, Literal, Union

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, TypeAdapter, ValidationError

__stub_keep__ = ["AgentOutputError"]

FEEDBACK_PREFIX = "Invalid action. Fix these errors and reply with JSON only: "


class SearchAction(BaseModel):
    type: Literal["search"]
    query: str = Field(min_length=1)
    top_k: int = Field(default=5, ge=1, le=20)


class CalculatorAction(BaseModel):
    type: Literal["calculator"]
    expression: str


class FinalAnswer(BaseModel):
    type: Literal["final_answer"]
    answer: str
    citations: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)


class AgentOutputError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, attempts: int, last_error: ValidationError) -> None:
        super().__init__(f"no valid action after {attempts} attempt(s)")
        self.attempts = attempts
        self.last_error = last_error


def build_action_adapter(*models: type[BaseModel]) -> TypeAdapter[Any]:
    if not models:
        raise ValueError("need at least one action model")
    seen: dict[str, str] = {}
    for model in models:
        field = model.model_fields.get("type")
        if field is None or typing.get_origin(field.annotation) is not Literal:
            raise TypeError(f"{model.__name__}.type must be a Literal")
        for tag in typing.get_args(field.annotation):
            if tag in seen:
                raise ValueError(f"tag {tag!r} used by {seen[tag]} and {model.__name__}")
            seen[tag] = model.__name__
    return TypeAdapter(Annotated[Union[models], Field(discriminator="type")])  # noqa: UP007


def parse_actions(
    items: list[Any], adapter: TypeAdapter[Any]
) -> tuple[list[Any], list[tuple[int, ValidationError]]]:
    actions: list[Any] = []
    failures: list[tuple[int, ValidationError]] = []
    for i, item in enumerate(items):
        try:
            actions.append(adapter.validate_python(item))
        except ValidationError as err:
            failures.append((i, err))
    return actions, failures


def _feedback(err: ValidationError) -> str:
    parts = [
        f"{'.'.join(str(p) for p in e['loc']) or '(root)'}: {e['msg']}"
        for e in err.errors(include_url=False)
    ]
    return FEEDBACK_PREFIX + "; ".join(parts)


def next_action(
    call_llm: Callable[[list[dict[str, str]]], str],
    messages: list[dict[str, str]],
    adapter: TypeAdapter[Any],
    max_attempts: int = 3,
) -> Any:
    if max_attempts < 1:
        raise ValueError("max_attempts must be >= 1")
    history = list(messages)
    last_error: ValidationError | None = None
    for _ in range(max_attempts):
        raw = call_llm(list(history))
        try:
            return adapter.validate_json(raw)
        except ValidationError as err:
            last_error = err
            history += [
                {"role": "assistant", "content": raw},
                {"role": "user", "content": _feedback(err)},
            ]
    assert last_error is not None
    raise AgentOutputError(max_attempts, last_error) from last_error

Asynchronous Programming

Sequential vs concurrent embedding calls★☆☆ · ex01_concurrent_embeddings

Problem

fake_embed(text, delay) (given) simulates an I/O-bound embedding API call: it records the text in the module-level list CALLS when its body starts running, sleeps delay seconds with asyncio.sleep, and returns a tiny "vector" [float(len(text))].

  1. async def embed_sequential(texts) -> list of vectors, one await fake_embed(t) after another. Total time ~ sum of delays.

  2. async def embed_concurrent(texts) -> same result, but all calls run concurrently with asyncio.gather. Total time ~ max delay. Results MUST be in input order even though the calls finish in a different order. delays is an optional list (same length as texts) of per-text delays passed to fake_embed; when None use the default delay. Empty input -> [].

  3. def start_prefetch(texts) - a plain (non-async) function that must be called while an event loop is running. It schedules one Task per text with asyncio.create_task (name each task "embed-<index>") and returns the list of tasks WITHOUT awaiting them. The caller awaits them later.

  4. def embed_blocking_entrypoint(texts) - a plain function for scripts/CLIs that runs embed_concurrent(texts) on a fresh event loop and returns the vectors (asyncio.run).

Interviewers look for

  • Calling a coroutine function only creates a coroutine object - nothing runs until it is awaited or wrapped in a Task. Awaiting coroutines one by one is still sequential!
  • gather() returns results in the order of its arguments, not completion order.
  • create_task() schedules the coroutine on the loop immediately; it starts running at the caller's next suspension point (await) - not at the create_task line itself.
  • asyncio.run() creates a loop, runs one entry coroutine, then cancels leftovers and closes the loop. It cannot be called from inside a running loop (RuntimeError).

Work in exercises/py/16_async/ex01_concurrent_embeddings.py (or copy the starter code into any scratch file).

import asyncio
from collections.abc import Sequence
EMBED_DELAY = 0.05
CALLS: list[str] = []

async def fake_embed(text: str, delay: float=EMBED_DELAY) -> list[float]:
    """Pretend embedding API: I/O-bound, so it awaits instead of blocking."""
    CALLS.append(text)
    await asyncio.sleep(delay)
    return [float(len(text))]

async def embed_sequential(texts: Sequence[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
    raise NotImplementedError

async def embed_concurrent(texts: Sequence[str], delays: Sequence[float] | None=None) -> list[list[float]]:
    raise NotImplementedError

def start_prefetch(texts: Sequence[str]) -> list[asyncio.Task[list[float]]]:
    raise NotImplementedError

def embed_blocking_entrypoint(texts: Sequence[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
    raise NotImplementedError

import asyncio
from collections.abc import Sequence

__stub_keep__ = ["fake_embed"]

EMBED_DELAY = 0.05
CALLS: list[str] = []


async def fake_embed(text: str, delay: float = EMBED_DELAY) -> list[float]:
    """Pretend embedding API: I/O-bound, so it awaits instead of blocking."""
    CALLS.append(text)
    await asyncio.sleep(delay)
    return [float(len(text))]


async def embed_sequential(texts: Sequence[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
    return [await fake_embed(t) for t in texts]


async def embed_concurrent(texts: Sequence[str], delays: Sequence[float] | None = None) -> list[list[float]]:
    if delays is None:
        delays = [EMBED_DELAY] * len(texts)
    if len(delays) != len(texts):
        raise ValueError("delays must match texts")
    # gather wraps each coroutine in a Task, so they all run at once; order = argument order
    return await asyncio.gather(*(fake_embed(t, d) for t, d in zip(texts, delays, strict=True)))


def start_prefetch(texts: Sequence[str]) -> list[asyncio.Task[list[float]]]:
    # create_task needs a running loop (RuntimeError otherwise) - this is a sync helper
    # that is only valid when called from inside a coroutine.
    return [asyncio.create_task(fake_embed(t), name=f"embed-{i}") for i, t in enumerate(texts)]


def embed_blocking_entrypoint(texts: Sequence[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
    return asyncio.run(embed_concurrent(texts))

Fix the blocked event loop (debug)★★☆ · ex02_unblock_the_loop

Problem

A teammate's FastAPI-style service "uses async" but requests still pile up. This is their code - find why, then write the fixed versions below:

async def count_tokens_all(texts):
    return [legacy_count_tokens(t) for t in texts]     # sync, ~50 ms each

async def wait_until_ready(probe, *, interval, timeout):
    start = time.monotonic()
    while not await probe():
        if time.monotonic() - start > timeout:
            raise TimeoutError
        time.sleep(interval)

MODEL_READY = False                                     # global flag + polling
async def handle(prompt):
    while not MODEL_READY:
        await asyncio.sleep(0.001)
    ...

  1. async def count_tokens_all(texts) -> list[int] - legacy_count_tokens (given) is a blocking, synchronous library call you cannot rewrite. Run the calls in worker threads (asyncio.to_thread) concurrently, so the event loop stays responsive and the total time is ~one call, not the sum. Results in input order.

  2. async def wait_until_ready(probe, *, interval, timeout) -> int - probe is an async callable returning bool (e.g. a health check). Poll it every interval seconds WITHOUT blocking the loop. Return the number of probe calls it took. If it is not ready within timeout seconds raise TimeoutError.

  3. class WarmupGate - replace the global-flag busy-poll with an asyncio.Event: * open() - mark the model as loaded; wakes every waiter at once * is_open - property, bool * async wait(timeout=None) -> bool - wait until open; return True, or False if timeout (seconds) elapses first (do not raise).

Interviewers look for

  • The event loop is single-threaded: any sync call that doesn't return quickly (time.sleep, requests.get, a heavy CPU loop, a sync DB driver) freezes EVERY coroutine on that loop.
  • asyncio.sleep suspends only the current coroutine; time.sleep blocks the thread.
  • asyncio.to_thread / loop.run_in_executor for blocking I/O; a process pool for heavy CPU work (the GIL still serialises pure-Python CPU work in threads).
  • Event = broadcast "this happened" signal; no polling, no wasted wake-ups.

import asyncio
import time
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable, Sequence

__stub_keep__ = ["legacy_count_tokens"]

TOKENIZE_DELAY = 0.05


def legacy_count_tokens(text: str) -> int:
    """A blocking sync library call (think: a C tokenizer or a sync HTTP client)."""
    time.sleep(TOKENIZE_DELAY)
    return len(text.split())


async def count_tokens_all(texts: Sequence[str]) -> list[int]:
    return list(await asyncio.gather(*(asyncio.to_thread(legacy_count_tokens, t) for t in texts)))


async def wait_until_ready(probe: Callable[[], Awaitable[bool]], *, interval: float, timeout: float) -> int:
    calls = 0

    async def _poll() -> None:
        nonlocal calls
        while True:
            calls += 1
            if await probe():
                return
            await asyncio.sleep(interval)  # yields to the loop - other requests keep flowing

    async with asyncio.timeout(timeout):  # raises TimeoutError (builtin) on expiry
        await _poll()
    return calls


class WarmupGate:
    """Requests wait here until the model has finished loading."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._event = asyncio.Event()

    def open(self) -> None:
        self._event.set()

    @property
    def is_open(self) -> bool:
        return self._event.is_set()

    async def wait(self, timeout: float | None = None) -> bool:
        try:
            async with asyncio.timeout(timeout):
                await self._event.wait()
        except TimeoutError:
            return False
        return True

Partial failures in a batch of LLM calls★★☆ · ex03_partial_failures

Problem

embed arguments below are async callables embed(text) -> list[float] that may raise (rate limits, timeouts, bad input...).

  1. async def embed_partial(texts, embed) -> BatchReport - call embed for every text concurrently with asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True). One bad text must not lose the other results: * BatchReport.vectors[i] is the vector for texts[i], or None if that call failed * BatchReport.errors maps index -> the exception instance raised for that text * only Exception subclasses count as per-item errors. If gather hands back a non-Exception BaseException (e.g. a CancelledError of a child), re-raise it - never report cancellation as "just a failed item".

  2. async def embed_with_retries(texts, embed, *, rounds) -> BatchReport - like embed_partial, but after each round re-run ONLY the still-failed indices (concurrently), up to rounds total rounds (rounds >= 1, else ValueError). Errors in the report are the ones from the last attempt of each still-failing index.

  3. async def embed_all_or_nothing(texts, embed) -> list[list[float]] - all-or-nothing semantics: start every call as a Task and wait with asyncio.wait(tasks, return_when=asyncio.FIRST_EXCEPTION). As soon as one call fails, cancel every still-pending task, wait until they have actually finished cancelling (so their finally: blocks ran), then raise the exception of the failed call (if several failed in the same wake-up, the one with the lowest index). On success return vectors in input order. Note plain gather() would propagate the first error but leave the siblings running in the background.

Interviewers look for

  • gather() without return_exceptions: the FIRST exception propagates to the awaiter, but the other awaitables are NOT cancelled - they keep running (and their errors may be "never retrieved").
  • return_exceptions=True puts exception objects in the result list -> you must type-check every element.
  • cancel() only requests cancellation; you must await the task to know it finished.

Work in exercises/py/16_async/ex03_partial_failures.py (or copy the starter code into any scratch file).

import asyncio
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable, Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
Vector = list[float]
Embed = Callable[[str], Awaitable[Vector]]

@dataclass
class BatchReport:
    vectors: list[Vector | None]
    errors: dict[int, Exception] = field(default_factory=dict)

async def embed_partial(texts: Sequence[str], embed: Embed) -> BatchReport:
    raise NotImplementedError

async def embed_with_retries(texts: Sequence[str], embed: Embed, *, rounds: int) -> BatchReport:
    raise NotImplementedError

async def embed_all_or_nothing(texts: Sequence[str], embed: Embed) -> list[Vector]:
    raise NotImplementedError

import asyncio
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable, Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

Vector = list[float]
Embed = Callable[[str], Awaitable[Vector]]


@dataclass
class BatchReport:
    vectors: list[Vector | None]
    errors: dict[int, Exception] = field(default_factory=dict)


async def embed_partial(texts: Sequence[str], embed: Embed) -> BatchReport:
    results = await asyncio.gather(*(embed(t) for t in texts), return_exceptions=True)
    report = BatchReport(vectors=[None] * len(texts))
    for i, r in enumerate(results):
        if isinstance(r, Exception):
            report.errors[i] = r
        elif isinstance(r, BaseException):
            raise r  # CancelledError / KeyboardInterrupt are not "item failures"
        else:
            report.vectors[i] = r
    return report


async def embed_with_retries(texts: Sequence[str], embed: Embed, *, rounds: int) -> BatchReport:
    if rounds < 1:
        raise ValueError("rounds must be >= 1")
    report = BatchReport(vectors=[None] * len(texts))
    todo = list(range(len(texts)))
    for _ in range(rounds):
        if not todo:
            break
        attempt = await embed_partial([texts[i] for i in todo], embed)
        still_failing: list[int] = []
        for pos, idx in enumerate(todo):
            if pos in attempt.errors:
                report.errors[idx] = attempt.errors[pos]
                still_failing.append(idx)
            else:
                report.vectors[idx] = attempt.vectors[pos]
                report.errors.pop(idx, None)
        todo = still_failing
    return report


async def embed_all_or_nothing(texts: Sequence[str], embed: Embed) -> list[Vector]:
    if not texts:
        return []
    tasks = [asyncio.create_task(embed(t)) for t in texts]
    try:
        done, pending = await asyncio.wait(tasks, return_when=asyncio.FIRST_EXCEPTION)
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        # we were cancelled ourselves: don't leak the children
        for t in tasks:
            t.cancel()
        await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)
        raise
    failed = [t for t in tasks if t in done and not t.cancelled() and t.exception() is not None]
    if failed:
        for t in pending:
            t.cancel()
        # wait for the cancellations to complete; return_exceptions so CancelledError
        # of the children doesn't propagate out of this gather
        await asyncio.gather(*pending, return_exceptions=True)
        exc = failed[0].exception()
        assert exc is not None
        raise exc
    return [t.result() for t in tasks]

Timeouts, fallbacks and a latency budget★★☆ · ex04_timeouts_and_budgets

Problem

call arguments are zero-arg async callables (e.g. lambda: llm.complete(prompt)).

  1. async def call_with_fallback(call, *, timeout, fallback) - use asyncio.wait_for. Return the call's result, or fallback if it takes longer than timeout seconds. Only the timeout is handled: any other exception from call propagates unchanged. (The timed-out call must be cancelled - wait_for does that for you.)

  2. async def retry_with_timeout(call, *, attempts, per_attempt_timeout, backoff=0.0) - each attempt gets its own timeout. Retry on TimeoutError and ConnectionError; any other exception propagates immediately. Sleep backoff * 2**k seconds before retry number k+1 (k = 0, 1, ...). After attempts failed attempts re-raise the LAST error. attempts < 1 -> ValueError.

  3. async def answer_within_budget(question, *, retrieve, generate, budget) -> Answer - a RAG request with ONE latency budget shared by both steps (use asyncio.timeout): docs = await retrieve(question) # -> list[str] text = await generate(question, docs) # -> str * finished in time -> Answer(text, docs, timed_out=False) * budget exceeded at any step -> Answer(FALLBACK_TEXT, docs retrieved so far (or []), timed_out=True) * if the caller cancels this coroutine, the CancelledError must propagate - do not turn an outer cancellation into a fallback answer.

Interviewers look for

  • A timeout is implemented as cancellation: the inner coroutine receives CancelledError at its current await, so its finally/cleanup runs - then the timeout surfaces as TimeoutError (builtin TimeoutError; asyncio.TimeoutError is an alias since 3.11).
  • Per-call timeouts vs an overall deadline: three 2 s steps each with a 2 s timeout can take 6 s; asyncio.timeout() around the whole block enforces a single budget.
  • Never except BaseException/bare except around awaits: you'd swallow CancelledError.

Work in exercises/py/16_async/ex04_timeouts_and_budgets.py (or copy the starter code into any scratch file).

import asyncio
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any
FALLBACK_TEXT = 'Sorry, that took too long - please try again.'

@dataclass
class Answer:
    text: str
    docs: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    timed_out: bool = False

async def call_with_fallback[T](call: Callable[[], Awaitable[T]], *, timeout: float, fallback: T) -> T:
    raise NotImplementedError

async def retry_with_timeout[T](call: Callable[[], Awaitable[T]], *, attempts: int, per_attempt_timeout: float, backoff: float=0.0) -> T:
    raise NotImplementedError

async def answer_within_budget(question: str, *, retrieve: Callable[[str], Awaitable[list[str]]], generate: Callable[[str, list[str]], Awaitable[str]], budget: float) -> Answer:
    raise NotImplementedError

import asyncio
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

FALLBACK_TEXT = "Sorry, that took too long - please try again."


@dataclass
class Answer:
    text: str
    docs: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    timed_out: bool = False


async def call_with_fallback[T](call: Callable[[], Awaitable[T]], *, timeout: float, fallback: T) -> T:
    try:
        return await asyncio.wait_for(call(), timeout)
    except TimeoutError:
        return fallback


async def retry_with_timeout[T](
    call: Callable[[], Awaitable[T]],
    *,
    attempts: int,
    per_attempt_timeout: float,
    backoff: float = 0.0,
) -> T:
    if attempts < 1:
        raise ValueError("attempts must be >= 1")
    last: Exception | None = None
    for k in range(attempts):
        if k and backoff:
            await asyncio.sleep(backoff * 2 ** (k - 1))
        try:
            return await asyncio.wait_for(call(), per_attempt_timeout)
        except (TimeoutError, ConnectionError) as e:
            last = e
    assert last is not None
    raise last


async def answer_within_budget(
    question: str,
    *,
    retrieve: Callable[[str], Awaitable[list[str]]],
    generate: Callable[[str, list[str]], Awaitable[str]],
    budget: float,
) -> Answer:
    docs: list[Any] = []
    try:
        async with asyncio.timeout(budget):
            docs = await retrieve(question)
            text = await generate(question, docs)
    except TimeoutError:
        # only OUR deadline becomes TimeoutError; an outer cancel stays CancelledError
        return Answer(FALLBACK_TEXT, docs, timed_out=True)
    return Answer(text, docs)

Bounded concurrency and an async token bucket★★☆ · ex05_rate_limits

Problem

LLM providers limit you two ways: max concurrent requests, and requests per second.

  1. async def bounded_map(fn, items, *, limit) -> list - apply the async fn to every item concurrently, but with at most limit calls in flight at any moment (asyncio.Semaphore). Results in input order. limit < 1 -> ValueError (raise it before starting any work). If one call raises, the exception propagates (gather semantics are fine).

  2. class TokenBucket(rate, capacity) - an async rate limiter: * the bucket starts full with capacity tokens and refills continuously at rate tokens/second, never above capacity * async acquire(tokens=1) waits (asyncio.sleep, never time.sleep) until tokens are available, then takes them. tokens > capacity -> ValueError (it could never succeed); rate <= 0 or capacity < 1 -> ValueError in init * many coroutines call acquire() concurrently: no more tokens may be handed out than the bucket allows, and waiters are served in FIFO order - guard the refill/check/take sequence with an asyncio.Lock (hold it while waiting, so later callers queue up). * use the event loop clock: asyncio.get_running_loop().time()

Interviewers look for

  • Semaphore limits concurrency (in-flight), a token bucket limits throughput (rate); production clients usually need both.
  • async with sem: releases even when the call raises or is cancelled.
  • asyncio.Lock is not thread-safe and isn't reentrant; it's needed when a critical section contains an await (otherwise single-threaded asyncio code can't interleave there).
  • Check-then-act across an await is the classic asyncio race.

Work in exercises/py/16_async/ex05_rate_limits.py (or copy the starter code into any scratch file).

import asyncio
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable, Iterable

async def bounded_map[T, R](fn: Callable[[T], Awaitable[R]], items: Iterable[T], *, limit: int) -> list[R]:
    raise NotImplementedError

class TokenBucket:

    def __init__(self, rate: float, capacity: int) -> None:
        raise NotImplementedError

    async def acquire(self, tokens: int=1) -> None:
        raise NotImplementedError

import asyncio
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable, Iterable


async def bounded_map[T, R](fn: Callable[[T], Awaitable[R]], items: Iterable[T], *, limit: int) -> list[R]:
    if limit < 1:
        raise ValueError("limit must be >= 1")
    sem = asyncio.Semaphore(limit)

    async def run(item: T) -> R:
        async with sem:
            return await fn(item)

    return list(await asyncio.gather(*(run(i) for i in items)))


class TokenBucket:
    def __init__(self, rate: float, capacity: int) -> None:
        if rate <= 0 or capacity < 1:
            raise ValueError("rate must be > 0 and capacity >= 1")
        self.rate = rate
        self.capacity = capacity
        self._tokens = float(capacity)
        self._updated: float | None = None  # loop clock is only available inside a loop
        self._lock = asyncio.Lock()

    async def acquire(self, tokens: int = 1) -> None:
        if tokens > self.capacity:
            raise ValueError("tokens exceeds bucket capacity")
        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        async with self._lock:  # FIFO: asyncio.Lock wakes waiters in arrival order
            while True:
                now = loop.time()
                if self._updated is not None:
                    elapsed = now - self._updated
                    self._tokens = min(self.capacity, self._tokens + elapsed * self.rate)
                self._updated = now
                if self._tokens >= tokens:
                    self._tokens -= tokens
                    return
                # sleep exactly until enough tokens will have accrued; others wait on the lock
                await asyncio.sleep((tokens - self._tokens) / self.rate)

Streaming: token streams, pagination, as_completed★★☆ · ex06_streaming

Problem

  1. async def stream_tokens(text, *, delay=0.005) - an ASYNC GENERATOR that fakes an LLM streaming response: yield each whitespace-separated word of text, awaiting asyncio.sleep(delay) before each one. When the generator finishes OR is closed early (consumer breaks + aclose(), or is cancelled), append text to the module-level list STREAMS_CLOSED exactly once (try/finally).

  2. async def collect_until(stream, stop) -> str - consume an async iterable of tokens with async for, joining them with single spaces, stopping BEFORE the first token equal to stop (a "stop sequence"). After stopping early you must close the stream: call await stream.aclose() if it has that method (don't rely on garbage collection).

  3. class Paginator(fetch_page) - an async ITERATOR class (implement __aiter__ and __anext__, no async generator) over a paginated vector-search API. fetch_page(cursor) is async, takes None for the first page and returns a Page (given). Iterate over the individual hits across all pages, fetching each page lazily (only when the previous page's hits are used up). Stop when a page has next_cursor is None and its hits are consumed. Empty pages in the middle are allowed.

  4. async def relevant_ids(hits, min_score) -> list[str] - use an ASYNC COMPREHENSION to return the id of every hit from the async iterable hits with score >= min_score.

  5. async def as_they_finish(calls) - an async generator: run the zero-arg async callables in calls concurrently and yield (index, result) pairs in COMPLETION order using asyncio.as_completed. If the consumer stops early, cancel the calls that are still running (finally) - no orphaned tasks.

Interviewers look for

  • An async generator is async def + yield; consume with async for, it has aclose() / asend() / athrow().
  • Async iterator protocol: __aiter__ (plain def, returns self) + async __anext__ raising StopAsyncIteration.
  • Early break from async for does NOT run the generator's finally right away - close it explicitly (or contextlib.aclosing), or the cleanup happens at GC / loop shutdown.
  • as_completed yields futures in completion order; you lose the input index unless you carry it in the result.

import asyncio
from collections.abc import AsyncIterable, AsyncIterator, Awaitable, Callable, Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

STREAMS_CLOSED: list[str] = []


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Hit:
    id: str
    score: float


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Page:
    hits: list[Hit] = field(default_factory=list)
    next_cursor: str | None = None


async def stream_tokens(text: str, *, delay: float = 0.005) -> AsyncIterator[str]:
    try:
        for word in text.split():
            await asyncio.sleep(delay)
            yield word
    finally:
        STREAMS_CLOSED.append(text)


async def collect_until(stream: AsyncIterable[str], stop: str) -> str:
    out: list[str] = []
    try:
        async for tok in stream:
            if tok == stop:
                break
            out.append(tok)
    finally:
        aclose = getattr(stream, "aclose", None)
        if aclose is not None:
            await aclose()
    return " ".join(out)


class Paginator:
    def __init__(self, fetch_page: Callable[[str | None], Awaitable[Page]]) -> None:
        self._fetch = fetch_page
        self._buffer: list[Hit] = []
        self._cursor: str | None = None
        self._started = False
        self._exhausted = False

    def __aiter__(self) -> "Paginator":
        return self

    async def __anext__(self) -> Hit:
        while not self._buffer:
            if self._exhausted:
                raise StopAsyncIteration
            page = await self._fetch(self._cursor if self._started else None)
            self._started = True
            self._buffer = list(page.hits)
            self._cursor = page.next_cursor
            self._exhausted = page.next_cursor is None
        return self._buffer.pop(0)


async def relevant_ids(hits: AsyncIterable[Hit], min_score: float) -> list[str]:
    return [h.id async for h in hits if h.score >= min_score]


async def as_they_finish[T](calls: Sequence[Callable[[], Awaitable[T]]]) -> AsyncIterator[tuple[int, T]]:
    async def tagged(i: int, call: Callable[[], Awaitable[T]]) -> tuple[int, T]:
        return i, await call()

    tasks = [asyncio.create_task(tagged(i, c)) for i, c in enumerate(calls)]
    try:
        for fut in asyncio.as_completed(tasks):
            yield await fut
    finally:
        for t in tasks:
            t.cancel()
        await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)
How did it go?
Racing replicas, hedged requests, deadlines★★★ · ex07_hedged_requests

Problem

calls / call are zero-arg async callables (e.g. the same prompt sent to different LLM providers or replicas). All three functions use asyncio.wait.

  1. async def first_success(calls) -> tuple[int, T] - start all calls at once and return (index, result) of the first one to SUCCEED (FIRST_COMPLETED in a loop: a call that fails is ignored while others are still running). Before returning, cancel all the losers and wait for them to finish cancelling. If every call fails raise ExceptionGroup("all calls failed", errors) with the errors in INDEX order. Empty calls -> ValueError.

  2. async def hedged(call, *, hedge_after, max_attempts=2) -> T - "tail-latency hedging" (Google's The Tail at Scale): start one attempt; every time hedge_after seconds pass with no attempt finished, start one more copy (up to max_attempts running copies). Return the first successful result and cancel the rest (await them). If an attempt fails, start a replacement immediately if the attempt budget allows, otherwise keep waiting for the others; if all max_attempts attempts failed re-raise the last error.

  3. async def gather_within(calls, *, deadline) -> tuple[dict[int, T], list[int]] - the "multi-retriever" pattern: run all calls, wait at most deadline seconds (ALL_COMPLETED with a timeout - note asyncio.wait does NOT raise on timeout), then cancel whatever is still pending. Return (results, late) where results maps index -> result for calls that finished successfully in time and late is the sorted list of indices that had to be cancelled. Calls that raised are left out of both (log-and-skip).

Interviewers look for

  • asyncio.wait returns two SETS (done, pending) of tasks - it never raises the tasks' exceptions and never cancels anything for you; mapping back to inputs is your job.
  • Pass Tasks, not coroutines, to asyncio.wait (coroutines are rejected since 3.11).
  • Cancel losers AND await them: "fire-and-forget cancel" leaves work running / connections open and produces "Task was destroyed but it is pending" warnings.
  • Hedging trades a little extra load for a much better p99.

Work in exercises/py/16_async/ex07_hedged_requests.py (or copy the starter code into any scratch file).

import asyncio
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable, Sequence
type Call[T] = Callable[[], Awaitable[T]]

async def first_success[T](calls: Sequence[Call[T]]) -> tuple[int, T]:
    raise NotImplementedError

async def hedged[T](call: Call[T], *, hedge_after: float, max_attempts: int=2) -> T:
    raise NotImplementedError

async def gather_within[T](calls: Sequence[Call[T]], *, deadline: float) -> tuple[dict[int, T], list[int]]:
    raise NotImplementedError

import asyncio
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable, Sequence

type Call[T] = Callable[[], Awaitable[T]]


async def _cancel_all(tasks: set[asyncio.Task]) -> None:
    for t in tasks:
        t.cancel()
    await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)


async def first_success[T](calls: Sequence[Call[T]]) -> tuple[int, T]:
    if not calls:
        raise ValueError("need at least one call")
    index: dict[asyncio.Task, int] = {}
    for i, c in enumerate(calls):
        index[asyncio.create_task(c())] = i  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    pending: set[asyncio.Task] = set(index)
    errors: dict[int, Exception] = {}
    try:
        while pending:
            done, pending = await asyncio.wait(pending, return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
            winners = sorted((index[t], t) for t in done if t.exception() is None)
            for t in done:
                if (exc := t.exception()) is not None:
                    errors[index[t]] = exc  # type: ignore[assignment]
            if winners:
                i, task = winners[0]
                return i, task.result()
    finally:
        await _cancel_all(pending)  # also runs if WE are cancelled
    raise ExceptionGroup("all calls failed", [errors[i] for i in sorted(errors)])


async def hedged[T](call: Call[T], *, hedge_after: float, max_attempts: int = 2) -> T:
    if max_attempts < 1:
        raise ValueError("max_attempts must be >= 1")
    running: set[asyncio.Task] = set()
    started = 0
    last_error: Exception | None = None

    def launch() -> None:
        nonlocal started
        running.add(asyncio.create_task(call()))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        started += 1

    launch()
    try:
        while running:
            timeout = hedge_after if started < max_attempts else None
            done, _ = await asyncio.wait(running, timeout=timeout, return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
            if not done:  # hedge timer fired: nobody answered yet -> send a backup request
                launch()
                continue
            running -= done
            for t in done:
                if t.exception() is None:
                    return t.result()
                last_error = t.exception()  # type: ignore[assignment]
            if started < max_attempts:
                launch()
    finally:
        await _cancel_all(running)
    assert last_error is not None
    raise last_error


async def gather_within[T](calls: Sequence[Call[T]], *, deadline: float) -> tuple[dict[int, T], list[int]]:
    if not calls:
        return {}, []
    tasks = [asyncio.create_task(c()) for c in calls]  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    done, pending = await asyncio.wait(tasks, timeout=deadline, return_when=asyncio.ALL_COMPLETED)
    await _cancel_all(pending)
    results = {i: t.result() for i, t in enumerate(tasks) if t in done and t.exception() is None}
    late = sorted(i for i, t in enumerate(tasks) if t in pending)
    return results, late

Ingestion pipeline: Queue, workers, graceful shutdown★★★ · ex08_queue_pipeline

Problem

embed(text) arguments are async callables returning a vector; they may raise.

  1. async def ingest(source, embed, *, workers=3, maxsize=10) -> IngestReport source is an ASYNC iterable of (doc_id, text) pairs (e.g. rows streamed from a DB). * one producer copies source into an asyncio.Queue(maxsize) - the bounded queue gives BACKPRESSURE: the producer must not run ahead of the workers by more than the queue size * workers worker tasks take items and call embed; success -> report.vectors[doc_id], an Exception -> report.failed[doc_id] = the exception (the worker keeps going) * when the source is exhausted and every item is processed, shut the workers down cleanly (sentinels, or queue.join() + cancel) and return. No task may outlive the call. * if the source itself raises, stop the workers and propagate that exception * workers < 1 or maxsize < 1 -> ValueError

  2. class IngestService(embed, *, workers=2) - a long-running version with lifecycle: * async start() - spawn the worker tasks * async submit(doc_id, text) - enqueue (unbounded queue); RuntimeError if the service is not started or is stopping/stopped * async stop(*, drain=True, timeout=None):

    • drain=True: stop accepting work, wait until everything already queued is processed, then stop the workers. If timeout is given and draining takes longer, fall back to a hard stop.
    • drain=False (hard stop): cancel the workers right away. After a hard stop, cancelled lists doc_ids whose embed call was interrupted mid-flight (record it in the worker's CancelledError handler, then RE-RAISE) and dropped lists queued-but-never-started doc_ids in queue order. When stop() returns, all worker tasks are finished.
    • attributes: vectors: dict, failed: dict, cancelled: list, dropped: list

Interviewers look for

  • Bounded queue = backpressure; an unbounded queue just moves the OOM somewhere else.
  • queue.task_done() once per get() (in a finally!) or join() hangs forever.
  • Shutdown options: sentinels (one per worker), join() then cancel, or Queue.shutdown() (3.13+). Graceful = stop intake -> drain -> stop workers -> await them; with a timeout that escalates to cancellation (what Kubernetes' SIGTERM -> SIGKILL grace period expects).
  • A worker that swallows CancelledError can never be stopped.

import asyncio
from collections.abc import AsyncIterable, Awaitable, Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

Vector = list[float]
Embed = Callable[[str], Awaitable[Vector]]


@dataclass
class IngestReport:
    vectors: dict[str, Vector] = field(default_factory=dict)
    failed: dict[str, Exception] = field(default_factory=dict)


_STOP = object()


async def ingest(
    source: AsyncIterable[tuple[str, str]], embed: Embed, *, workers: int = 3, maxsize: int = 10
) -> IngestReport:
    if workers < 1 or maxsize < 1:
        raise ValueError("workers and maxsize must be >= 1")
    queue: asyncio.Queue[object] = asyncio.Queue(maxsize)
    report = IngestReport()

    async def worker() -> None:
        while True:
            item = await queue.get()
            try:
                if item is _STOP:
                    return
                doc_id, text = item  # type: ignore[misc]
                try:
                    report.vectors[doc_id] = await embed(text)
                except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - per-item failure, keep going
                    report.failed[doc_id] = e
            finally:
                queue.task_done()

    tasks = [asyncio.create_task(worker()) for _ in range(workers)]
    try:
        async for item in source:
            await queue.put(item)  # blocks while the queue is full -> backpressure
        for _ in tasks:
            await queue.put(_STOP)  # FIFO: sentinels arrive after all real items
        await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
    finally:
        # on error (or our own cancellation) don't leave workers behind
        for t in tasks:
            t.cancel()
        await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)
    return report


class IngestService:
    def __init__(self, embed: Embed, *, workers: int = 2) -> None:
        self._embed = embed
        self._n_workers = workers
        self._queue: asyncio.Queue[tuple[str, str]] = asyncio.Queue()
        self._workers: list[asyncio.Task[None]] = []
        self._accepting = False
        self.vectors: dict[str, Vector] = {}
        self.failed: dict[str, Exception] = {}
        self.cancelled: list[str] = []
        self.dropped: list[str] = []

    async def start(self) -> None:
        self._workers = [
            asyncio.create_task(self._work(), name=f"ingest-{i}") for i in range(self._n_workers)
        ]
        self._accepting = True

    async def submit(self, doc_id: str, text: str) -> None:
        if not self._accepting:
            raise RuntimeError("service is not accepting work")
        await self._queue.put((doc_id, text))

    async def _work(self) -> None:
        while True:
            doc_id, text = await self._queue.get()
            try:
                self.vectors[doc_id] = await self._embed(text)
            except asyncio.CancelledError:
                self.cancelled.append(doc_id)
                raise  # never swallow: that's what lets stop() actually stop us
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
                self.failed[doc_id] = e
            finally:
                self._queue.task_done()

    async def stop(self, *, drain: bool = True, timeout: float | None = None) -> None:
        self._accepting = False
        if drain:
            try:
                async with asyncio.timeout(timeout):
                    await self._queue.join()
            except TimeoutError:
                pass  # escalate to a hard stop below
        for t in self._workers:
            t.cancel()
        await asyncio.gather(*self._workers, return_exceptions=True)
        while not self._queue.empty():
            doc_id, _ = self._queue.get_nowait()
            self._queue.task_done()
            self.dropped.append(doc_id)

Structured concurrency: TaskGroup and a task DAG★★★ · ex09_taskgroup_dag

Problem

  1. async def enrich_chunk(chunk, *, summarize, keywords, embed) -> Enriched Run the three async calls on chunk concurrently inside an asyncio.TaskGroup and return Enriched(summary, keywords, vector). If any call fails the TaskGroup cancels the others and raises an ExceptionGroup - let it propagate (don't catch it).

  2. async def run_dag(nodes) -> dict[str, Any] nodes maps name -> Node(deps, fn) (given). fn is async and receives ONE argument: a dict {dep_name: dep_result} of its direct dependencies. Run the whole graph inside a TaskGroup with maximum parallelism: every node starts as soon as ALL of its own deps have finished (not "level by level" - a node must not wait for unrelated slow nodes). Return {name: result} for every node. * validate BEFORE running anything: a dep that isn't a node, or a cycle -> ValueError * if a node fails: every running node is cancelled, nodes not yet started never start, and the TaskGroup's ExceptionGroup propagates Typical use: an agent plan "fetch_profile, fetch_orders -> build_prompt -> llm".

Interviewers look for

  • TaskGroup (3.11+) = structured concurrency: no task outlives the async with block; the first failure cancels siblings; errors surface as ExceptionGroup (handle with except*).
  • gather() vs TaskGroup: gather leaves siblings running on error (unless return_exceptions), TaskGroup cancels them. A Task can be awaited by many waiters (that's how deps work).
  • Dependencies: await the dependency tasks inside each node's coroutine; topological order only for creating tasks / detecting cycles.

class Node:

    deps: tuple[str, ...] = field(default=())

import asyncio
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable, Mapping
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from graphlib import CycleError, TopologicalSorter
from typing import Any


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Enriched:
    summary: str
    keywords: list[str]
    vector: list[float]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Node:
    fn: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], Awaitable[Any]]
    deps: tuple[str, ...] = field(default=())


async def enrich_chunk(
    chunk: str,
    *,
    summarize: Callable[[str], Awaitable[str]],
    keywords: Callable[[str], Awaitable[list[str]]],
    embed: Callable[[str], Awaitable[list[float]]],
) -> Enriched:
    async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg:
        s = tg.create_task(summarize(chunk))
        k = tg.create_task(keywords(chunk))
        v = tg.create_task(embed(chunk))
    # leaving the block means all three finished successfully
    return Enriched(s.result(), k.result(), v.result())


async def run_dag(nodes: Mapping[str, Node]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    for name, node in nodes.items():
        missing = [d for d in node.deps if d not in nodes]
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(f"{name!r} depends on unknown node(s) {missing}")
    try:
        order = list(TopologicalSorter({n: node.deps for n, node in nodes.items()}).static_order())
    except CycleError as e:
        raise ValueError(f"dependency cycle: {e.args[1]}") from e

    tasks: dict[str, asyncio.Task[Any]] = {}

    async def run(name: str) -> Any:
        node = nodes[name]
        # deps were created earlier (topological order), so their tasks exist
        dep_results = {d: await tasks[d] for d in node.deps}
        return await node.fn(dep_results)

    async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg:
        for name in order:
            tasks[name] = tg.create_task(run(name), name=name)
    return {name: t.result() for name, t in tasks.items()}
How did it go?
Embedding micro-batcher (Condition + async with)★★★ · ex10_micro_batcher

Problem

Embedding APIs are far cheaper per text when called with a batch, but requests arrive one at a time from many concurrent handlers. Build the classic server-side micro-batcher.

class MicroBatcher(embed_batch, *, max_batch, max_wait) * embed_batch(texts: list[str]) -> list[vector] is async, one vector per text, in order. * async embed(text) -> vector - called concurrently by many coroutines. Each call adds its text to a pending list and waits for ITS vector (an asyncio.Future per request is the usual trick). * A single background flusher task (started by __aenter__) sends batches: - as soon as max_batch texts are pending -> flush immediately - otherwise flush whatever is pending max_wait seconds after the FIRST text of the batch arrived (a lone request must not wait forever) - never more than max_batch texts per call; record every batch size, in order, in the batch_sizes list attribute Use an asyncio.Condition to let embed() wake the flusher, and don't hold the condition's lock while awaiting embed_batch (new requests must keep queueing). * If embed_batch raises, every caller in THAT batch gets the exception; the batcher keeps serving later batches. * async with MicroBatcher(...) as b: - __aenter__ starts the flusher and returns self; __aexit__ calls aclose(). * async aclose() - graceful: refuse new work, flush everything still pending (without waiting for max_wait), then stop the flusher task and await it. Idempotent. embed() after close -> RuntimeError.

Interviewers look for

  • Condition = Lock + "wait until predicate"; await cond.wait_for(pred) re-checks after every notify and re-acquires the lock before returning (also when cancelled/timed out).
  • Size-or-time flushing is exactly how vLLM/TGI continuous batching and embedding services trade a few ms of latency for big throughput gains.
  • Futures connect a producer-side result to an awaiting caller; guard against callers that were cancelled (fut.done()) before setting a result.
  • Async context managers make start/stop symmetric and exception-safe.

Work in exercises/py/16_async/ex10_micro_batcher.py (or copy the starter code into any scratch file).

import asyncio
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
Vector = list[float]

class MicroBatcher:

    def __init__(self, embed_batch: Callable[[list[str]], Awaitable[list[Vector]]], *, max_batch: int, max_wait: float) -> None:
        raise NotImplementedError

    async def __aenter__(self) -> 'MicroBatcher':
        raise NotImplementedError

    async def __aexit__(self, *exc_info: object) -> None:
        raise NotImplementedError

    async def embed(self, text: str) -> Vector:
        raise NotImplementedError

    async def aclose(self) -> None:
        raise NotImplementedError

import asyncio
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable

Vector = list[float]


class MicroBatcher:
    def __init__(
        self,
        embed_batch: Callable[[list[str]], Awaitable[list[Vector]]],
        *,
        max_batch: int,
        max_wait: float,
    ) -> None:
        if max_batch < 1 or max_wait < 0:
            raise ValueError("max_batch must be >= 1 and max_wait >= 0")
        self._embed_batch = embed_batch
        self.max_batch = max_batch
        self.max_wait = max_wait
        self.batch_sizes: list[int] = []
        self._pending: list[tuple[str, asyncio.Future[Vector]]] = []
        self._cond = asyncio.Condition()
        self._closing = False
        self._task: asyncio.Task[None] | None = None

    async def __aenter__(self) -> "MicroBatcher":
        self._task = asyncio.create_task(self._flusher(), name="micro-batcher")
        return self

    async def __aexit__(self, *exc_info: object) -> None:
        await self.aclose()

    async def embed(self, text: str) -> Vector:
        if self._closing or self._task is None:
            raise RuntimeError("batcher is not running")
        fut: asyncio.Future[Vector] = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_future()
        async with self._cond:
            self._pending.append((text, fut))
            self._cond.notify()
        return await fut

    async def _next_batch(self) -> list[tuple[str, asyncio.Future[Vector]]] | None:
        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        async with self._cond:
            await self._cond.wait_for(lambda: self._pending or self._closing)
            if not self._pending:
                return None  # closing and nothing left
            deadline = loop.time() + self.max_wait
            try:
                async with asyncio.timeout_at(deadline):
                    await self._cond.wait_for(lambda: len(self._pending) >= self.max_batch or self._closing)
            except TimeoutError:
                pass  # time's up: flush a partial batch
            batch = self._pending[: self.max_batch]
            del self._pending[: self.max_batch]
            return batch

    async def _flusher(self) -> None:
        while (batch := await self._next_batch()) is not None:
            self.batch_sizes.append(len(batch))
            try:
                vectors = await self._embed_batch([t for t, _ in batch])
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - deliver to the waiting callers
                for _, fut in batch:
                    if not fut.done():
                        fut.set_exception(e)
                continue
            for (_, fut), vec in zip(batch, vectors, strict=True):
                if not fut.done():  # the caller may have been cancelled meanwhile
                    fut.set_result(vec)

    async def aclose(self) -> None:
        if self._task is None or self._task.done():
            self._closing = True
            return
        async with self._cond:
            self._closing = True
            self._cond.notify_all()
        await self._task  # flusher drains the backlog, then returns

Async HTTP and API Integration

httpx basics: Client, AsyncClient, GET/POST★☆☆ · ex01_http_basics

http.requests_vs_httpx, http.concurrent_calls

Problem

A small client for an OpenAI-style API at API_BASE. No real network: every function takes a client (or a transport) so tests can inject httpx.MockTransport.

  1. make_client(api_key, *, transport=None) -> httpx.Client

    • base_url=API_BASE, headers: "Authorization: Bearer <key>", "User-Agent: USER_AGENT"
    • timeout = httpx.Timeout(10.0, connect=2.0)
    • pass transport through (None means the real network transport)

  2. list_models(client) -> list[str]

    • GET /models -> {"data": [{"id": "gpt-4o"}, ...]} -> the ids, sorted
    • any non-2xx status -> httpx.HTTPStatusError (hint: response.raise_for_status())

  3. search(client, query, top_k=5) -> list[dict]

    • GET /search with query parameters q=<query>, k=<top_k> - let httpx encode them (never build "?q=" + query by hand: "refund & returns" must arrive intact)
    • returns response.json()["results"]; non-2xx -> httpx.HTTPStatusError

  4. create_embeddings(client, texts, model="text-embedding-3-small") -> list[list[float]]

    • POST /embeddings with JSON body {"model": model, "input": texts}
    • response {"data": [{"index": i, "embedding": [...]}, ...]} - return the vectors in INPUT order (sort by "index"; servers don't promise list order)
    • non-2xx -> httpx.HTTPStatusError

  5. async fetch_documents(client: httpx.AsyncClient, doc_ids) -> list[dict | None]

    • GET /documents/{id} for every id CONCURRENTLY (not one after another)
    • results in the same order as doc_ids; a 404 gives None in that slot; any other non-2xx raises httpx.HTTPStatusError

Interviewers look for

  • A Client is a connection pool + shared config (base_url, headers, timeouts): create it once, reuse it; httpx.get(...) per call opens a new connection each time.
  • requests is sync-only; httpx has the same API for sync (Client) and async (AsyncClient), plus HTTP/2, strict timeouts by default (5 s) and a pluggable transport (MockTransport).
  • Sync I/O blocks the thread; with AsyncClient + gather, N requests take ~max(latency) instead of sum(latency).
  • GET = safe/idempotent query (params in the URL); POST = create/compute (JSON body).

import asyncio
from typing import Any

import httpx

API_BASE = "https://api.example.com/v1"
USER_AGENT = "rag-service/1.0"


def make_client(api_key: str, *, transport: httpx.BaseTransport | None = None) -> httpx.Client:
    return httpx.Client(
        base_url=API_BASE,
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}", "User-Agent": USER_AGENT},
        timeout=httpx.Timeout(10.0, connect=2.0),
        transport=transport,
    )


def list_models(client: httpx.Client) -> list[str]:
    response = client.get("/models")
    response.raise_for_status()
    return sorted(item["id"] for item in response.json()["data"])


def search(client: httpx.Client, query: str, top_k: int = 5) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    response = client.get("/search", params={"q": query, "k": top_k})
    response.raise_for_status()
    return response.json()["results"]


def create_embeddings(
    client: httpx.Client, texts: list[str], model: str = "text-embedding-3-small"
) -> list[list[float]]:
    response = client.post("/embeddings", json={"model": model, "input": texts})
    response.raise_for_status()
    items = sorted(response.json()["data"], key=lambda item: item["index"])
    return [item["embedding"] for item in items]


async def _fetch_one(client: httpx.AsyncClient, doc_id: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    response = await client.get(f"/documents/{doc_id}")
    if response.status_code == 404:
        return None
    response.raise_for_status()
    return response.json()


async def fetch_documents(client: httpx.AsyncClient, doc_ids: list[str]) -> list[dict[str, Any] | None]:
    # gather preserves argument order regardless of completion order
    return await asyncio.gather(*(_fetch_one(client, doc_id) for doc_id in doc_ids))

Status codes -> typed API exceptions★☆☆ · ex02_status_errors

Problem

SDKs like openai/anthropic turn HTTP failures into a typed exception hierarchy so callers can write except RateLimitError: instead of inspecting status codes everywhere. The hierarchy below is given.

  1. parse_retry_after(value, now=None) -> float | None Retry-After is either delta-seconds ("2", "0.5") or an HTTP-date ("Wed, 21 Oct 2015 07:28:00 GMT").

    • seconds -> float(value); negative -> None
    • HTTP-date -> seconds from now (default: datetime.now(UTC)) until that date, never below 0.0
    • None / empty / unparseable -> None (hint: email.utils.parsedate_to_datetime raises on garbage - catch TypeError/ValueError)

  2. error_message(response) -> str Best human-readable message from an error body:

    • JSON {"error": {"message": "..."}} -> that message
    • JSON {"error": "..."} or {"detail": "..."} or {"message": "..."} (checked in that order, value must be a str)
    • otherwise the stripped response text, cut to 200 characters
    • empty body -> f"HTTP {status_code}"

  3. raise_for_api_error(response) -> httpx.Response

    • status < 400 -> return the response unchanged
    • otherwise raise (message=error_message(response), status_code, request_id from the "x-request-id" header or None): 400, 422 -> BadRequestError 401 -> AuthenticationError 403 -> PermissionDeniedError 404 -> NotFoundError 409 -> ConflictError 429 -> RateLimitError (with retry_after parsed from the Retry-After header) >= 500 -> InternalServerError any other 4xx -> APIStatusError

  4. send(client, method, url, **kwargs) -> httpx.Response

    • client.request(...), then raise_for_api_error
    • httpx.TimeoutException -> APITimeoutError; any other httpx.TransportError -> APIConnectionError; chain the original (raise ... from exc)

  5. is_retryable(exc: APIError) -> bool

    • True for connection errors (incl. timeouts), RateLimitError, InternalServerError, and APIStatusError with status 408 or 409; False for everything else (400, 401, 403, 404, 422 will fail again exactly the same way)

Interviewers look for

  • 4xx = the client's fault (fix the request; don't retry) - except 408/409/429; 5xx = the server's fault (often transient, retry with backoff).
  • 401 (who are you?) vs 403 (I know you, but no); 400 (malformed) vs 422 (well-formed but semantically invalid); 429 carries Retry-After.
  • Keep the request id in the exception - it's what the provider's support asks for.
  • Preserve the cause chain (from exc) so tracebacks show the transport error.

from typing import Any
import httpx

class APIError(Exception):

    def __init__(self, message: str, *, status_code: int | None=None, request_id: str | None=None):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.message = message
        self.status_code = status_code
        self.request_id = request_id

class APIStatusError(APIError):
    """Any non-2xx response."""

class BadRequestError(APIStatusError):
    ...

class AuthenticationError(APIStatusError):
    ...

class PermissionDeniedError(APIStatusError):
    ...

class NotFoundError(APIStatusError):
    ...

class ConflictError(APIStatusError):
    ...

class RateLimitError(APIStatusError):

    def __init__(self, message: str, *, retry_after: float | None=None, **kwargs: Any):
        super().__init__(message, **kwargs)
        self.retry_after = retry_after

class InternalServerError(APIStatusError):
    ...

class APIConnectionError(APIError):
    """The request never got a response (DNS, refused, reset, timeout...)."""

class APITimeoutError(APIConnectionError):
    ...

def parse_retry_after(value: str | None, now: datetime | None=None) -> float | None:
    raise NotImplementedError

def error_message(response: httpx.Response) -> str:
    raise NotImplementedError

def raise_for_api_error(response: httpx.Response) -> httpx.Response:
    raise NotImplementedError

def send(client: httpx.Client, method: str, url: str, **kwargs: Any) -> httpx.Response:
    raise NotImplementedError

def is_retryable(exc: APIError) -> bool:
    raise NotImplementedError

from datetime import UTC, datetime
from email.utils import parsedate_to_datetime
from typing import Any

import httpx

__stub_keep__ = [
    "APIError",
    "APIStatusError",
    "BadRequestError",
    "AuthenticationError",
    "PermissionDeniedError",
    "NotFoundError",
    "ConflictError",
    "RateLimitError",
    "InternalServerError",
    "APIConnectionError",
    "APITimeoutError",
]


class APIError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message: str, *, status_code: int | None = None, request_id: str | None = None):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.message = message
        self.status_code = status_code
        self.request_id = request_id


class APIStatusError(APIError):
    """Any non-2xx response."""


class BadRequestError(APIStatusError): ...


class AuthenticationError(APIStatusError): ...


class PermissionDeniedError(APIStatusError): ...


class NotFoundError(APIStatusError): ...


class ConflictError(APIStatusError): ...


class RateLimitError(APIStatusError):
    def __init__(self, message: str, *, retry_after: float | None = None, **kwargs: Any):
        super().__init__(message, **kwargs)
        self.retry_after = retry_after


class InternalServerError(APIStatusError): ...


class APIConnectionError(APIError):
    """The request never got a response (DNS, refused, reset, timeout...)."""


class APITimeoutError(APIConnectionError): ...


def parse_retry_after(value: str | None, now: datetime | None = None) -> float | None:
    if not value or not value.strip():
        return None
    value = value.strip()
    try:
        seconds = float(value)
    except ValueError:
        pass
    else:
        return seconds if seconds >= 0 else None
    try:
        when = parsedate_to_datetime(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    now = now or datetime.now(UTC)
    return max(0.0, (when - now).total_seconds())


def error_message(response: httpx.Response) -> str:
    try:
        body = response.json()
    except ValueError:  # json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError
        body = None
    if isinstance(body, dict):
        err = body.get("error")
        if isinstance(err, dict) and isinstance(err.get("message"), str):
            return err["message"]
        for key in ("error", "detail", "message"):
            if isinstance(body.get(key), str):
                return body[key]
    text = response.text.strip()
    return text[:200] if text else f"HTTP {response.status_code}"


def raise_for_api_error(response: httpx.Response) -> httpx.Response:
    status = response.status_code
    if status < 400:
        return response
    kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {
        "status_code": status,
        "request_id": response.headers.get("x-request-id"),
    }
    message = error_message(response)
    if status == 429:
        raise RateLimitError(
            message, retry_after=parse_retry_after(response.headers.get("retry-after")), **kwargs
        )
    match status:
        case 400 | 422:
            cls: type[APIStatusError] = BadRequestError
        case 401:
            cls = AuthenticationError
        case 403:
            cls = PermissionDeniedError
        case 404:
            cls = NotFoundError
        case 409:
            cls = ConflictError
        case _ if status >= 500:
            cls = InternalServerError
        case _:
            cls = APIStatusError
    raise cls(message, **kwargs)


def send(client: httpx.Client, method: str, url: str, **kwargs: Any) -> httpx.Response:
    try:
        response = client.request(method, url, **kwargs)
    except httpx.TimeoutException as exc:
        raise APITimeoutError(f"request timed out: {exc}") from exc
    except httpx.TransportError as exc:
        raise APIConnectionError(f"connection error: {exc}") from exc
    return raise_for_api_error(response)


def is_retryable(exc: APIError) -> bool:
    if isinstance(exc, (APIConnectionError, RateLimitError, InternalServerError)):
        return True
    return isinstance(exc, APIStatusError) and exc.status_code in (408, 409)

A reusable async API client★★☆ · ex03_async_client

http.request_timeouts, http.response_validation, http.get_post, http.error_handling

Problem

EmbeddingsClient wraps ONE httpx.AsyncClient for its whole lifetime:

async with EmbeddingsClient("https://api.example.com/v1", api_key) as ec:
    resp = await ec.embed(["a", "b"])        # -> EmbeddingResponse (pydantic)

The response models and exceptions are given.

init(base_url, api_key, *, timeout=None, max_connections=10, transport=None) * only stores configuration - no client yet (constructors shouldn't do I/O) * self.timeout = timeout or DEFAULT_TIMEOUT (30 s overall, 5 s to connect) * self.limits = httpx.Limits(max_connections=max_connections, max_keepalive_connections=max_connections)

async aenter -> self * creates the httpx.AsyncClient (base_url, "Authorization: Bearer <key>" header, timeout, limits, transport). Entering twice without exiting -> RuntimeError. async aexit * closes the client (aclose) - even if the body raised - and forgets it

client (property) -> httpx.AsyncClient * the open client; RuntimeError("client is not open") outside async with

async embed(texts, model="text-embedding-3-small", *, timeout=None) -> EmbeddingResponse * POST /embeddings {"model": model, "input": texts} * timeout (float seconds) overrides the client timeout for THIS request only * httpx.ConnectTimeout -> APITimeoutError(phase="connect"); any other httpx.TimeoutException -> APITimeoutError(phase="read") (chain the cause) * status >= 400 -> APIStatusError(status_code, body text) * body not valid JSON, or not matching EmbeddingResponse -> ResponseValidationError (chain the cause; keep the raw text in .raw) * len(data) != len(texts), or indices not exactly 0..n-1 -> ResponseValidationError * the returned response's data is sorted by index

async health() -> bool * GET /health; True iff status 200. Transport errors/timeouts -> False (never raise).

Interviewers look for

  • One AsyncClient per process/component: it owns a connection POOL; creating a client per request throws away keep-alive connections (new TCP + TLS handshake every call) and leaks sockets if not closed.
  • httpx.Limits bounds pool size; pool timeout is how long you wait for a free connection.
  • Timeout phases: connect (can we reach the host?), read (time between bytes), write, pool. A ConnectTimeout means the request was never sent - a ReadTimeout means it might have been processed (matters for retrying POSTs).
  • Validate responses at the boundary: a 200 with a garbage body is still a failure.

        self.status_code = status_code
        self.body = body

class APITimeoutError(Exception):

class ResponseValidationError(Exception):

        raise NotImplementedError

from typing import Any, Self

import httpx
from pydantic import BaseModel, ValidationError

__stub_keep__ = ["APIStatusError", "APITimeoutError", "ResponseValidationError"]

DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = httpx.Timeout(30.0, connect=5.0)


class EmbeddingItem(BaseModel):
    index: int
    embedding: list[float]


class Usage(BaseModel):
    prompt_tokens: int
    total_tokens: int


class EmbeddingResponse(BaseModel):
    model: str
    data: list[EmbeddingItem]
    usage: Usage


class APIStatusError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, status_code: int, body: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(f"HTTP {status_code}: {body[:200]}")
        self.status_code = status_code
        self.body = body


class APITimeoutError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, phase: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(f"{phase} timeout")
        self.phase = phase


class ResponseValidationError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message: str, raw: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.raw = raw


class EmbeddingsClient:
    def __init__(
        self,
        base_url: str,
        api_key: str,
        *,
        timeout: httpx.Timeout | None = None,
        max_connections: int = 10,
        transport: httpx.AsyncBaseTransport | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.base_url = base_url
        self.timeout = timeout or DEFAULT_TIMEOUT
        self.limits = httpx.Limits(
            max_connections=max_connections, max_keepalive_connections=max_connections
        )
        self._api_key = api_key
        self._transport = transport
        self._client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None

    async def __aenter__(self) -> Self:
        if self._client is not None:
            raise RuntimeError("client already open")
        self._client = httpx.AsyncClient(
            base_url=self.base_url,
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {self._api_key}"},
            timeout=self.timeout,
            limits=self.limits,
            transport=self._transport,
        )
        return self

    async def __aexit__(self, *exc_info: object) -> None:
        client, self._client = self._client, None
        if client is not None:
            await client.aclose()

    @property
    def client(self) -> httpx.AsyncClient:
        if self._client is None:
            raise RuntimeError("client is not open - use 'async with'")
        return self._client

    async def embed(
        self, texts: list[str], model: str = "text-embedding-3-small", *, timeout: float | None = None
    ) -> EmbeddingResponse:
        extra: dict[str, Any] = {} if timeout is None else {"timeout": timeout}
        try:
            response = await self.client.post(
                "/embeddings", json={"model": model, "input": texts}, **extra
            )
        except httpx.ConnectTimeout as exc:
            raise APITimeoutError("connect") from exc
        except httpx.TimeoutException as exc:
            raise APITimeoutError("read") from exc
        if response.status_code >= 400:
            raise APIStatusError(response.status_code, response.text)
        try:
            parsed = EmbeddingResponse.model_validate_json(response.content)
        except ValidationError as exc:  # covers invalid JSON too
            raise ResponseValidationError(f"bad embeddings response: {exc}", response.text) from exc
        indices = sorted(item.index for item in parsed.data)
        if indices != list(range(len(texts))):
            raise ResponseValidationError(
                f"expected indices 0..{len(texts) - 1}, got {indices}", response.text
            )
        parsed.data.sort(key=lambda item: item.index)
        return parsed

    async def health(self) -> bool:
        try:
            response = await self.client.get("/health")
        except httpx.TransportError:
            return False
        return response.status_code == 200
