Streaming LLM responses: parsing Server-Sent Events★★☆ · ex06_sse_streaming

Problem

Chat APIs stream tokens as Server-Sent Events over HTTP. The network hands you arbitrary byte chunks: a chunk can end in the middle of a line - or in the middle of a multi-byte UTF-8 character.

data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"role":"assistant"}}]}
&lt;blank line>
data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Hel"}}]}
&lt;blank line>
: keep-alive comment
data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"lo"},"finish_reason":"stop"}]}
&lt;blank line>
data: [DONE]

  1. async iter_sse_data(chunks) -> AsyncIterator[str] chunks: AsyncIterable[bytes]. Yield the payload of every "data:" line, in order. * lines end with "\n" or "\r\n"; a line may be split across chunks; decode UTF-8 incrementally (codecs.getincrementaldecoder) - never chunk.decode() per chunk * payload = text after "data:", with ONE leading space removed if present * ignore blank lines, comment lines (starting with ":") and other fields (event:, id:, retry:) - one data line = one event in this exercise * payload "[DONE]" -> stop immediately: don't yield it, don't pull more chunks * a final line without a trailing newline is still processed at end of stream

  2. async stream_text(chunks) -> AsyncIterator[str] On top of iter_sse_data: json.loads each payload and yield payload["choices"][0]["delta"]["content"] when it's a non-empty string (skip role-only deltas, null content, events with an empty choices list). A payload with an "error" key -> raise StreamError(payload["error"]["message"]).

  3. async collect_stream(chunks, on_delta=None) -> StreamResult Consume stream_text, call on_delta(delta) for each delta (if given), and return StreamResult(text="".join(deltas), finish_reason=<last non-null choices[0]["finish_reason"] seen, or None>, n_deltas=<number of deltas>). (Hint: finish_reason is only visible at the payload level - share a small helper between stream_text and collect_stream that yields (delta, finish_reason) pairs.)

Interviewers look for

  • Streaming improves time-to-first-token (perceived latency), not total latency.
  • Buffer bytes until a newline; decode incrementally - splitting "é" (2 bytes) across chunks makes per-chunk .decode() raise UnicodeDecodeError.
  • Async generators give back-pressure for free: nothing is read until the consumer asks.
  • Stop on [DONE]; surface mid-stream errors (the HTTP status was already 200!).
  • Production: also handle client disconnects (cancellation closes the generator) and timeouts between chunks.

Work in exercises/py/23_genai/ex06_sse_streaming.py (or copy the starter code into any scratch file).

class StreamResult:
    text: str
    finish_reason: str | None
    n_deltas: int

class StreamError(Exception):
    """The provider reported an error in the middle of the stream."""

async def iter_sse_data(chunks: AsyncIterable[bytes]) -> AsyncIterator[str]:
    raise NotImplementedError
    yield

async def stream_text(chunks: AsyncIterable[bytes]) -> AsyncIterator[str]:
    raise NotImplementedError
    yield

import codecs
import json
from collections.abc import AsyncIterable, AsyncIterator, Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class StreamResult:
    text: str
    finish_reason: str | None
    n_deltas: int


class StreamError(Exception):
    """The provider reported an error in the middle of the stream."""


def _payload(line: str) -> str | None:
    line = line.removesuffix("\r")
    if not line.startswith("data:"):
        return None  # blank, comment (":..."), or another field
    data = line[5:]
    return data[1:] if data.startswith(" ") else data


async def iter_sse_data(chunks: AsyncIterable[bytes]) -> AsyncIterator[str]:
    decoder = codecs.getincrementaldecoder("utf-8")()
    buffer = ""
    async for chunk in chunks:
        buffer += decoder.decode(chunk)
        *lines, buffer = buffer.split("\n")
        for line in lines:
            data = _payload(line)
            if data == "[DONE]":
                return
            if data is not None:
                yield data
    buffer += decoder.decode(b"", final=True)
    data = _payload(buffer)
    if data is not None and data != "[DONE]":
        yield data


async def _deltas(chunks: AsyncIterable[bytes]) -> AsyncIterator[tuple[str | None, str | None]]:
    async for data in iter_sse_data(chunks):
        event: dict[str, Any] = json.loads(data)
        if "error" in event:
            raise StreamError(event["error"].get("message", "unknown stream error"))
        choices = event.get("choices") or []
        if not choices:
            continue
        content = (choices[0].get("delta") or {}).get("content")
        yield (content if isinstance(content, str) and content else None), choices[0].get("finish_reason")


async def stream_text(chunks: AsyncIterable[bytes]) -> AsyncIterator[str]:
    async for delta, _ in _deltas(chunks):
        if delta:
            yield delta


async def collect_stream(
    chunks: AsyncIterable[bytes], on_delta: Callable[[str], object] | None = None
) -> StreamResult:
    parts: list[str] = []
    finish_reason: str | None = None
    async for delta, reason in _deltas(chunks):
        if reason is not None:
            finish_reason = reason
        if delta:
            parts.append(delta)
            if on_delta is not None:
                on_delta(delta)
    return StreamResult("".join(parts), finish_reason, len(parts))
How did it go?
Config from the environment, secrets that never leak★★☆ · ex07_settings_secrets

Problem

12-factor config: settings come from environment variables (optionally a .env file in dev), are validated at startup, and secrets never end up in logs, reprs or tracebacks.

  1. class Settings(BaseSettings) - the fields are given; you write the validators. env prefix "APP_" (APP_API_KEY, APP_MODEL, ...), case-insensitive, no .env file by default (pass _env_file=path to read one), unknown APP_* variables ignored. * api_key: SecretStr (required) * model: str = "small-chat" * temperature: float in [0, 2] * max_tokens: int > 0 * context_window: int > 0 * base_url: str * log_level: str = "INFO" Validators to write: * log_level (field validator): case-insensitive, stored upper-case, must be one of DEBUG/INFO/WARNING/ERROR/CRITICAL * check (model validator, mode="after"), runs on every instantiation:

    • max_tokens must be < context_window (leave room for the prompt)
    • base_url must start with "https://" - except http://localhost / http://127.0.0.1 for local dev Invalid config -> pydantic.ValidationError at startup (fail fast, not at first request).

  2. get_settings() -> Settings - cached with functools.lru_cache (one Settings object per process; tests call get_settings.cache_clear()).

  3. class RedactingFilter(logging.Filter) RedactingFilter(secrets: Iterable[str]) - attach it to a HANDLER. filter(record) renders the message (record.getMessage()), replaces every given secret (ignore empty strings) and anything that looks like an API key (regex: sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}) with "***", stores the result in record.msg and sets record.args = None. Always returns True (redact, never drop records).

  4. class JsonFormatter(logging.Formatter) - structured logs, one JSON object per line: format(record) -> json.dumps({"level": record.levelname, "logger": record.name, "message": record.getMessage(), **extras}) where extras are the attributes passed via extra={...} (= record.dict keys that a plain LogRecord doesn't have). If record.exc_info is set, add "exc": self.formatException(record.exc_info). Values that aren't JSON-serialisable are converted with str().

Interviewers look for

  • SecretStr: repr/str/model_dump show "**********"; .get_secret_value() only at the call site that needs it (the HTTP header).
  • Fail fast: validate config at startup; one cached Settings, injected where needed.
  • Precedence: init kwargs > env vars > .env file > defaults. Never commit .env; secrets come from a secret manager / CI secret store in prod.
  • Filters on a LOGGER don't see records propagated from child loggers; filters on the HANDLER see everything that handler emits - that's where redaction belongs.
  • Structured (JSON) logs with request_id/model/latency/tokens fields -> searchable, aggregatable, alertable; same fields go to error tracking (Sentry) as tags.

import json
import logging
import re
from collections.abc import Iterable
from functools import cache, lru_cache
from typing import Self

from pydantic import Field, SecretStr, field_validator, model_validator
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict

LEVELS = ("DEBUG", "INFO", "WARNING", "ERROR", "CRITICAL")
LOCAL_HTTP = ("http://localhost", "http://127.0.0.1")


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_prefix="APP_", env_file=None, extra="ignore", case_sensitive=False)

    api_key: SecretStr
    model: str = "small-chat"
    temperature: float = Field(0.2, ge=0.0, le=2.0)
    max_tokens: int = Field(1024, gt=0)
    context_window: int = Field(8192, gt=0)
    base_url: str = "https://api.example.com/v1"
    log_level: str = "INFO"

    @field_validator("log_level")
    @classmethod
    def normalize_level(cls, value: str) -> str:
        level = value.strip().upper()
        if level not in LEVELS:
            raise ValueError(f"log_level must be one of {LEVELS}")
        return level

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def check(self) -> Self:
        if self.max_tokens >= self.context_window:
            raise ValueError("max_tokens must be smaller than context_window")
        if not (self.base_url.startswith("https://") or self.base_url.startswith(LOCAL_HTTP)):
            raise ValueError("base_url must use https (http only for localhost)")
        return self


@lru_cache
def get_settings() -> Settings:
    return Settings()  # type: ignore[call-arg]  # values come from the environment


class RedactingFilter(logging.Filter):
    def __init__(self, secrets: Iterable[str]) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self._secrets = [s for s in secrets if s]
        self._key_pattern = re.compile(r"sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}")

    def filter(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> bool:
        message = record.getMessage()
        for secret in self._secrets:
            message = message.replace(secret, "***")
        record.msg = self._key_pattern.sub("***", message)
        record.args = None
        return True


@cache
def _standard_attrs() -> frozenset[str]:
    # everything a bare LogRecord has; anything else on a record came from `extra=`
    return frozenset(vars(logging.makeLogRecord({}))) | {"message", "asctime"}


class JsonFormatter(logging.Formatter):
    def format(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> str:
        payload = {
            "level": record.levelname,
            "logger": record.name,
            "message": record.getMessage(),
        }
        for key, value in vars(record).items():
            if key not in _standard_attrs():
                payload[key] = value
        if record.exc_info:
            payload["exc"] = self.formatException(record.exc_info)
        return json.dumps(payload, default=str)
